His own work is the hand: six answers, the sixty-seventh through the seventy-second — down at once, down before the letting-go, held to the river’s own interval, two rhythms crossed in the inch through one of Sella’s counted breaths and the silence after it, one rhythm held across that silence, and the crossing remembered. The last lies against the fold like a tool put away: exact, complete, worth nothing, not a reach, a hearing, a key, a power or a rule. He still cannot close two inches, lift the crust or speak a number. Nothing joined, paid, opened or ended; forward into Smoke 10 with the old life offstage.

Through Smoke 10–12 (Days 249–251) he is two hundred and forty-nine, fifty and fifty-one days old — six months and sixty-nine days to six months and seventy-one — and nobody tells him either figure. Smoke’s first Account-day and market comes on Smoke 10 and changes the district’s arithmetic for the first time in Smoke, unalterably, while nothing under the Vail roof is settled by it: the grain stays covered and unfigured, the read figure stays beside the paid figure with no signature between them, the five askings stay five with no witness, the ninth hand stays nine, the charcoal stays unread and the loan stays uncalled. Three counts in three places — the fire’s four pulls and missing fifth under the floor, its payer unnamed for 249, 250 and 251 days, the river’s note through the finger’s-width door, the boards’ four nails, four and a thumb-width knot — stay three, for agreeing any two would want a payer and none stands to any. The first smell is hot clay under tallow, wet wool under that, the sour Ash breath of the thaw; the first sound the kiln in fours with a gap, not a bell. Six hand questions are answered honestly, the seventy-third through the seventy-eighth, the last two rhythms crossing the inch across a wall that does not touch and remembered, not a change made again; seventy-eight objects lie on the sixth place, exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, and none is a reach, a hearing, a seventh, a payment, a key, a power or a rule. The body humiliates him as it has from the first: one stiff brown-edged crust two inches off with its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread frozen and unwiped, cold at cheek, temple and bare wrist-joint, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody will perform. He wants the crust and knows the face of a man going cold; both are true and the second is louder. The widow’s mark hangs where it hung, touched only before the kiln on Smoke 1 and looked at again as no sign, lesson, mending or payment; the seventh year stands at its very end and has not given. At the close the hand lays itself against the fold like a tool put away where the next hand will find it without looking, the fire stops at four, and 251 goes forward into Smoke 13, a day not yet earned. No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no new scar or possession, no power spent and no ending.

Through Smoke 13–15 (Days 252–254) he is two hundred and fifty-two, fifty-three and fifty-four days old — six months and seventy-two days to six months and seventy-four — and nobody tells him either figure. Smoke’s middle tend gathers and settles nothing: no market, no Cross and no bell on any of the three days, Smoke 20 (Day 259) five mornings beyond the close and not brought early. Three counts in three places — the fire’s four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should stand under the floor, its payer unnamed for two hundred and fifty-two, fifty-three and fifty-four days, the river’s note of water over water through the finger’s-width door, and the boards’ four nails, four and a thumb-width knot — stay three, for agreeing any two would want a payer and none stands to any. The surgeon takes the body’s inventory and enters it nowhere: one crust two inches off with its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread frozen and unwiped, cold at cheek, temple and bare wrist-joint, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody will perform; he knows the face of a man going cold and wants the crust, both true and the second louder. Six hand questions across the three days are answered honestly, the seventy-ninth through the eighty-fourth, the last a two-rhythm coordination across a wall that does not touch, remembered and not made again; eighty-four objects lie on the sixth place, exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, and none is a reach, a hearing, a seventh, a payment, a key, a power or a rule. On Smoke 14 a pot set down wrong at the racks gives its high thin note before its time and is swept around, and the sweet edge of lead glaze rides a wrong wind off High Kiln over the boards and goes out on it; both are filed and neither is spent. The ownerless question is not asked a sixth time and stands at five askings with no witness and no row named. The file is turned out on the towel at the close and found exact, complete and worth nothing; the hand is laid down against the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking. Forward, not closed.

On Smoke 16–18, Days 255–257, he is two hundred and fifty-five, then two hundred and fifty-six, then two hundred and fifty-seven days old — six months and seventy-five days to six months and seventy-seven — and nobody says either figure. The middle tend of the second firing asks nothing of him but the work already learned: the three counts in three places held apart, the body inventoried in its old order, the dressed grain turned under wool and then gathered in by the handful for the last time before Smoke’s second reading and set away from the hearth with no figure over it, and the frost on the well lip called weather by the yard and kept on a place of its own with no cause. The hand answers six times, the ninetieth holding an empty interval as an object in its own right without filling it to make a fifth stroke or crossing a second count; ninety honest answers stand on the sixth place and the file turned out on the towel is exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. He has still moved no Warm, gained no rank, made no payer and reached no seventh hearing; the surgeon’s register buys him the exact reading of what the child’s body cannot do, and the wanting of the crust is louder than the reading. Nothing in these three days is joined, named, opened, called, spent or ended, and Smoke 20 (Day 259) stands two mornings ahead, unearned and unbrought.

Through Smoke 19–21 he is two hundred and fifty-eight, then fifty-nine, then sixty days old, six months and seventy-eight through eighty days, told by nobody. Smoke’s second Account-day changes the district’s arithmetic a second time and cannot be changed back while the figure read over the covered grain at home does not know what it cost and the space between the two figures has no signature; the third working week begins as an ordinary tending that has learned nothing, and that nothing is itself a keeping. Six answers are filed on the sixth place, the ninety-first down at once on the river’s note, the ninety-second held for the small intake, the ninety-third held through the bell’s absent stroke and supplied with no stroke, the ninety-fourth carried across the silence in the room that does not touch, the ninety-fifth kept to the river’s own interval, and the ninety-sixth holding one rhythm for the small intake and a second, laid apart, across the little silence after a count that had ended in the other room. The file turned out on the towel is exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air; the widow’s mark hangs where it hangs, the charcoal stays unread, the ninth hand stays nine, the row question stays at five askings with no witness, the seventh year stands at its very end and has still not given, and Smoke 30 and the first firing of Frost stand ahead and unbrought (T071/T072, T088, T061/T082, T015/T041/T047, T077, T058/T079, T100, T080, T101, T036/T076, T006).

Through Smoke 22–24 he is two hundred and sixty-one, then sixty-two, then sixty-three days old, six months and eighty-one through eighty-three days, told by nobody. The third working week gathers toward Smoke’s last reading and settles nothing: no Account-day, market, Cross or bell, and Smoke 30 six mornings ahead and unbrought. In the plain work of the mornings he registers that the house keeps itself by \textbf{not-doings} --- two lines unswept, the mark untouched, the charcoal unread, the fifth pull unsupplied, the loan uncalled, no number spoken over the basket, the crust not lifted --- and keeps the seeing as a finding with no payer, not a grievance, a lesson or a doctrine. He does not lay the house’s omissions across his own kept empty intervals, for a joining would want a payer and none stands; the absence of the joining is itself kept. Six answers are filed on the sixth place, the ninety-seventh held for the small intake, the ninety-eighth through one whole interval of the river, the ninety-ninth down before the letting-go of a borrowed count, the hundredth carried across the little silence after a count in the room that does not touch, the hundred and first down on the river’s note and not on the kiln’s gap, and the hundred and second kept with the little silence after the house’s count left empty on its own place and not crossed. The file turned out on the towel is exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air; the three counts stay in three places, the widow’s mark hangs where it hangs, the ninth hand stays nine, the row question stays at five askings with no witness, the seventh year stands at its very end and has still not given, and Smoke 30 and the first firing of Frost stand ahead and unbrought (T071/T072, T088, T061/T082, T077, T080, T101, T058/T079, T100, T083/T085, T064, T036/T076, T006, T009/T013/T092, T098, T060/T086).

Through Smoke 25–27, Days 264–266, three more lived days under the Vail roof, the boy comes into his two hundred and sixty-sixth day with nobody telling him what the number would count and one hundred and eight honest answers standing on the sixth place. The third working week gathers toward Smoke’s last reading and settles nothing. The chapter’s finding is that a thing can be handled as closely as a hand can examine it and still enter nothing — Sella turns the dressed grain piece by piece for damp and rot on Smoke 26 — and the finding is kept on a place of its own, not a lesson, grievance or doctrine, not laid across the house’s not-doings or his own kept gaps, with a finger between and no payer named. Its physical counterpart is the hand on the hundred and eighth answer going on past the river’s next note to the one after it, holding two intervals with the silence between kept empty and no second house count borrowed, which he makes nothing of and will not let stand up as a gift. The ownerless row question gathers one further shaping, a report of an asking and not a sixth asking, with no witness and no row named; the ninth hand stays nine with Ilva’s strip unread. Tarn’s seventh year stands at its very end and has still not given; Jorra’s promise stays ungiven and \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed; Garl stays in objects with his name unspoken two hundred and sixty-six days. Nothing is joined, named, opened, called, spent or ended, and the count crosses into Smoke 28 unspent.

Through Frost 1–3, Days 270–272, three more lived days under the Vail roof, the boy comes into his two hundred and seventy-second day with nobody telling him what the number would count and one hundred and twenty honest answers standing on the sixth place. Frost comes on in its own light and goes out without a boundary drawn, and the month’s first firing on Frost 2 gives the chapter its one meaningful change: Sella goes to the kiln mouth before any word, holds the widow’s mark one breath, lifts the clay lid with the back of a hand and tips the coal under a broken pot, and the fire takes with its fifth still missing and its payer unnamed, nobody praising it or naming what it mended. He keeps the not-making as a finding with no payer, does not make four openings into a rule, and does not lay the household’s refusal across his own kept gaps, for a joining would want a payer and none stands; the rule of the mark is held exactly, with the touch at no other hour. On the last answer the hand sets a held interval beside an empty interval with a finger between and makes neither agree with the missing fifth, and the six answerings of these three days are exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. The grain stays covered and unfigured, the third arithmetic unread in Berr’s box; Tarn’s seventh year stands at its very end and has not given, Jorra’s promise stays ungiven, Ilva’s ninth hand stays nine, the row question stays at five with no witness, and Garl stays in objects with his name unspoken two hundred and seventy-two days. Nothing is joined, named, opened, called, spent or ended, and the count crosses into Frost 4 unspent.

Through Frost 4–6, Days 273–275, the working week begins by degrees and settles nothing. He comes into it two hundred and seventy-three days old and goes out of it two hundred and seventy-five — six months and ninety-three to six months and ninety-five days, nobody saying either figure. The count reaches two hundred and seventy-five exact with one hundred and twenty-six honest answers on the sixth place, and the six answers of these three days — a borrowed intake held, a letting-go left outside, one house rhythm carried across the little silence, two intakes held apart with a finger between, a separation made by ending early, and the held interval laid beside the empty interval — are exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. The chapter’s one change is Sella’s: on Frost 5 her finger goes beneath the loaf shelf and stays two counted breaths where it once stayed one, and comes away unread. He files it and forbids it to stand up as a cause, a payment, a gift or a rule. The first firing of Frost stays behind the household with no lesson or payer, four openings remain four, the grain stays covered and unfigured, the seven places go around with a look and no number, and nothing is joined, named, opened, called, paid or ended.

Through Frost 7–9, Days 276–278, the working week goes out as it came in and settles nothing. He comes into it two hundred and seventy-six days old and goes out of it two hundred and seventy-eight — six months and ninety-six to six months and ninety-eight days, nobody saying either figure. The count reaches two hundred and seventy-eight exact with one hundred and thirty-two honest answers on the sixth place, and the six answers of these three days — one house rhythm carried across the river’s interval with no fifth borrowed, an ending made early with the letting-go left whole, two intakes held apart with a finger between, a bridge laid between a counted breath’s intake and the next hold over the river’s note, a held interval set beside an empty interval, and the river’s own small intake set beside a counted hold — are exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. The chapter’s one meaningful change is the stayed frost: on Frost 8 the white the frost wrote on the well lip does not go when the sun is up as it went on Frost 4, and stays past noon and the going of the light onto Frost 9; the rope stiffens, the trough takes a skin and the coals are banked an hour earlier, and on Frost 9 Sella lifts a plate of ice and sets it out of the path of feet. The yard calls all of it weather, no figure is given, and nothing is made of it — no sign, lesson, mending, cause or payer, and Frost 10 does not pay it. He keeps each movement on a place of its own with a finger between and makes no fourth likeness a cause; the dressed grain is turned twice for damp and stays covered and unfigured, the seven places go around with a look and no number, and nothing is joined, named, opened, called, paid or ended.

Through Frost 10–12, Days 279–281, the count goes from two hundred and seventy-eight to \textbf{two hundred and eighty-one exact}, six months and ninety-nine days to six months and one hundred and one days told by nobody, with one hundred and thirty-eight honest answers on the sixth place and the fire’s fifth unpaid the same three days with its payer unnamed. The chapter’s one meaningful change is public and cannot be undone: Frost’s first Account-day comes to the Cross, Berr Clay reads \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says}, calls the levy and denies it with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, and goes off with the box locked and the first true subtraction of Frost inside, believing he has done a kindness; the district’s arithmetic changes for the month while the printed figure stands unchallenged, the figure read is still not the figure paid, and the reading knows nothing of the man carried out on Day 188, the hand that went in on Seed 15 or the dressed grain covered under wool at the rack end. Nothing of the reading comes back under the Vail roof as lesson, sign, mending, figure or payment. The six answers of these three days — a house rhythm carried across a counted silence, the heard bell’s gap set beside a held breath, a letting-go left whole, two intakes bridged over the river’s note, an intake held through the silence after its letting-go, and the held interval set beside the empty interval with a finger between — are exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. He keeps the stayed frost, the plate of ice, the covered grain and the house’s not-doings on places of their own apart from his own gaps, makes no fourth likeness a cause and no doctrine of four openings, and lets Frost 20 stand eight mornings ahead, unbrought. Nothing is joined, named, opened, called, paid or ended.

Through Frost 13–15, Days 282–284, the second working week is lived one dated day at a time and settles nothing. He comes into it two hundred and eighty-two days old and goes out of it two hundred and eighty-four — six months and one hundred and two days to six months and one hundred and four days, nobody saying either figure. Three counts stay in three places, the fire’s fifth unpaid through all three days with its payer unnamed, six hearings stay six with no seventh, and the body is inventoried in its old order and entered nowhere: one crust two inches off with its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread frozen and unwiped, cold at cheek, temple and wrist, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody will perform. The chapter’s one meaningful change is a saying arrived nowhere on the afternoon of Frost 14: a woman at the yard well, speaking to the boards and not into the basket, said that the runner who carries Berr Clay’s slate once carried a figure that named a person she knew. He takes it apart as a surgeon takes a wound apart and files it on a place of its own beside Hessa Rale’s eighth record-first hand with a finger between — a shaping toward the far-off day she must choose whether to read what she has carried, not a hearing, not a seventh, not a tenth hand, not a cause, not a confession, not a joining, not a witness and not paid. He does not make Hessa a reader and does not join the saying to Ilva’s strip a pace away, and one stray saying does not stand up as a rule, for a rule is an account that has found a payer and none stands. Six answers take the sixth place from one hundred and thirty-eight to one hundred and forty-four, the last setting the held interval beside the empty interval with a finger between and neither promoted; each is exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. The stayed frost, the plate of ice and the covered grain go forward unfigured, the row stays at five askings with no witness, Tarn’s seventh year stands at its very end and has not given, Jorra’s promise stays sealed, and Garl stays in objects with his name unspoken two hundred and eighty-four days. Nothing is joined, named, opened, called, paid or ended.

\item Ch 80: Lived Days 291–293, Frost 22–24, Secondday to Fourthday, three dated days in six scenes, two hundred and ninety-one through two hundred and ninety-three days old — six months and one hundred and eleven through one hundred and thirteen days — nobody saying either figure under any roof. Carried in a basket under the Vail roof, awake and silent; the surgeon’s inventory exact and useless and the infant’s want of the crust two inches off louder, the checking of satisfaction by want being the work and not a virtue. No present-tense Chicago break and no tagged remembered line. The hand filed six answers, the \textbf{one hundred and fifty-seventh} through the \textbf{one hundred and sixty-second}, each exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, the hundred and sixty-second setting the held interval beside the empty interval with a finger between and refusing to stand up as a doctrine, a gift or a rule; the count closed at \textbf{293 exact}. The six answers, 121 through 126, were honest coordinations on the sixth place: 121 took the small intake of a count from the room whose floor does not touch his and came down on the river’s note; 122 came down before that count’s letting-go and left the little silence after it whole; 123 stayed past a letting-go and through the silence, carrying one house rhythm across; 124 held two intakes apart with a finger between, the letting-go between them left where it was; 125 came down while the count was still letting go, a separation made by ending early and not by filling; 126 set the held interval and the empty interval side by side with a finger between and came down, taking nothing from the two-gapped row, the charcoal or the covered grain. All six were exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air — not reaches, hearings, sevenths, stoppings, payments, held changes, keys, powers, doctrines or rules (T061/T082). The seven walked-around places were gone around with a look and a wide step and no number on all three days, including the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, carried and not named (T009/T013/T092, T098). Tarn kept six where the house could check and the seventh at the knife’s lip, brought the ear-sentence to the calling word and stopped there as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled, no collector up or down the clay road (T036/T076, T006). Jorra parted dusty forearms from clean as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, spoke to the wheel and a pot before any person, withheld the note he knew three turns ahead, put his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence, gave the men who went low into the back room before first grey no name, kept the burned slate at four, the shut-room tellings at two and the three pot sayings with the Smoke 14 note apart, and neither gave nor withdrew the promise of the boy’s name (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095, T101, T064). Garl was kept in objects with his name unspoken two hundred and seventy-five days; Ilva was glimpsed once on Frost 5 at the well with clay pale in her nail crescents and grey rack dust in one thumb seam, her hand to her sleeve and the strip unread, answering \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account}, and the ninth hand stayed nine with a finger between it and the eighth (T080 held, not paid). The dressed grain lay under wool at the rack end, turned for damp with a lighter touch each morning and given no figure, the arithmetic that will read over it not knowing what it cost (T077). Nothing was joined, named, opened, called, paid, spent or ended; the file lay open on the towel with every gap left gap.

Three counts in three places — the carried fire’s four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should be under the floor (payer unnamed for two hundred and thirty-seven, thirty-eight and thirty-nine days, T088), the river’s note of water over water through the finger’s-width door, and the boards’ four nails, four and a thumb-width knot — none rising into another, for agreeing them would want a payer and none stands to any (T061/T082). One stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust lay two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread frozen and unwiped; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rode back, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, advanced and not paid:} on Day 239 Grain’s third arithmetic was read over the basket in the moot-post’s thin shade and cannot be changed back. Berr came up short off the clay road with the red wool cord folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, held a narrow slate unopened to his forearm, passed a finger over the figure and read \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says} low into the top of the crowd, the figure going twice over the basket, once for the moot and once for the households that came late; he said \emph{The levy is called. It is not called by me} and \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, taking himself out of his own sentence as a surgeon withdraws a hand before the dressing, and went off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness. The printed figure stood unchallenged and a figure read aloud was still not the figure paid; the reading answered nothing for the man carried out on Day 188 or the hand that went in on Seed 15 and did not come back (T015/T041/T047, T077, T098 carried). \textbf{The second advancement, paid nowhere:} on the afternoon of Day 238 the ownerless question came over the boards a \textbf{fourth} time, low into the boards and not into the basket, asking which row the pot went quiet on; the weather answered first and the price of barley after it, the voice went up the terrace toward High Kiln and the row stood where it stood, nobody leaning in to take the answer down. He opened it as a surgeon opens a wound — what it asks, where it stands, what it would want before any man could answer, who would stand under the answer to pay — and found no witness at the bottom; he set the fourth telling on the seventh place beside the first three with a finger between each pair and a finger between them and the sayings, the tellings, the hearings and the count. Four askings are still not one witness, for a witness stands somewhere and can be asked and none does and none could; not a fourth shaping, a hearing, a seventh of the full note, a fifth telling of the slate, a cause, a name or a fifth witness, and no fifth asking came (T101 advanced, unpaid). The file turned out as instruments on a towel in the small hours of Days 237 and 239 was exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth out of a person and no seventh, three near-full answers, three pot sayings, the fourth burned-slate telling and two shut-room tellings on their own places, told bell beside heard, told figure beside paid, nine stoppings with no tenth at the seventh year’s very end, three held changes plus the loft scrape, the pale line and the held inch, the seventh green a colour and the seventh shape a shape with no eighth of either, the dressed grain covered and unfigured, the returning-line place gone around with no number, and the question with four askings and no witness. Six answers across the six scenes — the \textbf{forty-ninth} down at once under conditions that had sometimes answered, the \textbf{fiftieth} held for the small intake and down before the letting-go, the \textbf{fifty-first} down before a counted breath had finished, the \textbf{fifty-second} held through a whole counted breath at Sella’s fire in the room that does not touch his and down with the breath, the \textbf{fifty-third} kept to the river’s own low interval and down on the next low note, and the \textbf{fifty-fourth} up an inch toward the low note through the finger’s-width door, carried through the small intake, the hold and the letting-go of one of Sella’s breaths, kept through the little silence after her count and down on the river’s next low note — two rhythms in one inch, remembered, not a change made again, not a longer reach, miss entered, hearing, seventh, tenth stopping, payment, held change, key, power or rule (T061/T082). The old life stayed offstage: no present-tense Chicago break, no `**` tag, no Court, collector or ending (T004). No new scar, possession or change of voice; Garl kept in objects with his name unspoken two hundred and thirty-nine days, no collector up or down the clay road on Grain 28, 29 or 30, and the count crosses into Smoke 1 exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody.

\item Ch 56: Days 219–221, Grain 10–12, Tenthday to Secondday, the first Account-day and market of Grain and two ordinary tending days, six lived scenes, each day opened by its own `\textbackslash{}daymark`. He is two hundred and nineteen, twenty and twenty-one days old — six months and thirty-nine days to six months and forty-one — and nobody says so (T071/T072); the count stays exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody, the carried fire’s fifth unpaid for the same three days (T088), and fire, river and boards keep three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). At the Cross on Day 219 he is set in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade where no slate lies; Berr reads one in twelve twice over the basket, calls the levy, denies it with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, and goes off with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he has done a kindness, while Hessa carries the slate up unread and the soft-cuffed clerk stays set at the out-of-line landing for an uncalled measure; the bell goes four, four and a gap, heard beside told, and the figure read is still not the figure paid (T015/T041/T047, T078, T080, T090). \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, paid as sightings only:} a seventh green comes to the mouth of a silent woman at the pot board — clay in the nail crescents, a pale line across the back of one hand where something was worn tight and long, sweet lead glaze in the crease beside her lip, a cup turned a quarter and set back exactly where it stood — and a seventh shape comes at the market’s edge — cast-offs with a man’s shoulders and breeches cut at the knee, silt pale in the wrist creases, a gap where a front tooth had been, the green sliver on its string catching light and going dull, the head going toward a set-down pot a half-beat late and stopping in the middle, no loaf, no slate, no sale. The first is filed as a colour (T050/T051 paid as a sighting), the second as a shape (T033/T034 paid as a sighting), never Fenna or Ulda in the narration, joined to no ear, cause, name or romance, with the sale to the Waiting Room clerk still years ahead. Across the three days he refuses to let the three shapings of the pot saying or the fourth burned-slate telling stand up as rules, keeps the two shut-room tellings at two and the nine stoppings with no tenth while the seventh year stands at its very end, and keeps the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled. The hand goes up an inch six times — down at once and short of a breath on the tenth, before the counted breath and then to the river’s note on the eleventh, at once under conditions that had answered and, on the twelfth, through one of the breaths Sella counts at her fire and the little silence after it, down on the river’s next low note — a two-rhythm coordination remembered, filed on the sixth place with no payer named; the private file turned out like instruments on a towel is exact, complete and worth nothing, and he still cannot close two inches, lift his chin to the crust or speak a number. No power, no rank change, no new scar or possession; the old life stays offstage and the count crosses into Day 222 unspent. Forward, not closed.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 1: Born in the front room of House Silt on Stone 7 and lived the whole day awake. Held the count of the floorboards, read Dessa’s pulse and sieve-wire scar, matched the pause in the dark hand on the birth-slate to the hand at the flare light and did not put them together, and felt the river stone go cold with nobody else in the room noticing. Wanted the breast more than he wanted the truth. Drooled, could not hold up his head, could not turn it past a point without a small animal sound, could not reach a cup, could not keep the wool on his shoulder. The clinical ear was wide awake and wholly useless.

\item Ch 2: Lived Days 2 and 3. Heard the flat note of a cup across the birth room for the first time and could neither reach the cup nor make anyone tap it; heard Des’s laugh break through in the present tense and go out; watched Alda cross the sign over his flower again without knowing it. Was carried up the Clay Yard in Sella’s bundle, counting her steps, while Alda told Dessa he had gone in the levy and the number was never spoken. Was laid on fresh straw under the Vail roof and given a bed while Tarn was given the loft; read the hollow seat, the salt coat and the Ash ridge as a man-shaped gap, and heard a second flat note from a pot without anyone naming it. The stone was left behind in House Silt; heat came back into his hands and feet; he was warmer and more watched and could say nothing about either.

\item Ch 3: Day 4, Account-day. Carried in a basket under wool from the Vail kiln-house down to the Cross, counting a hundred and nine steps and then the market’s pigs, turnips, hoops and bell. Heard \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says} spoken twice by Berr Clay and the Sill assessor’s \emph{the figure stands as read}, and stood inside the account that priced his kind without being named in it. Heard the slate’s flat note on the second and fourth hearings of the chapter --- a third vessel after the cup and the pot --- and could not lift a knuckle toward it. Ostrowski’s voice broke through in the present tense with the two duties; for one breath the market and the trauma bay were the same room; he reached for a pocket with no phone. Saw the neat hand’s stop a third time at the Court’s table, still unread. Heard Berr confirm Sella’s widow’s mark as a kindness that is entered, and knew the debt against the tiles was being spoken around. Watched Alda touch her tin, cross the sign at his wrist and cover it with a date; watched Mira ask the eel price and answer it herself without once looking at him; watched the barrow of Ash go out toward the north gate. Counted the bell four, four, a gap. Was carried back up the Clay Yard with no word spoken to him all day. Still mute, cracked, unranked, unable to read Grathic or lift a hand to his own chin.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 4: Lived Days 5 and 6. Heard the flat note a fourth time from a Vail pot through the wall and saw Tarn’s broom stop two strokes at it without a word; kept the hearing in its own place. Watched Alda reach for the slate before the child, touch the tin, cross the sign at the red edge of his wrist and write what she turned writing-down, while the neighbour’s rekindled child went grey at the fingertips and every woman corrected his knowledge of the Afterdrop with a kinder, older, wrong answer. Was carried to the Hearth Drawing in a basket set at the edge of the light; watched the collector’s cold iron tube find the place under a dying man’s arm, the exact hand that did not press, and heard the small flat knock a fifth time --- the first from a person --- and the soft sentence \emph{the measure is banked; the account stands; the return is recorded}. Knew the figure on the slate was the one the Cross had read aloud and could not reach the tube, read the writing or lift a knuckle toward it; the collector’s hand had no pause in it and he did not join it to the three. In the Chicago break the white light took the room for two sentences --- a nurse holding pressure, a hand going past a turned note toward a signature --- and went out. Reached for a pocket-place twice, found wool, did not look at the name. Kept the death-house ridge a finger’s width thicker than Vail’s, the Vail ridge, the charred slate and the barrow of grey side by side without joining them. Fed from the house’s own dish, unentered, with the coals banked, the fold put right without a look and the count four, four and a gap. Still six days old, mute, cracked, unranked, below Thin, with no power moved and nothing gained.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 5: Lived Days 7--9. On Stone 13 turned his head toward a pot \emph{before} Jorra set it down; the pot gave nothing and he kept the interval, count still five from four sources, while Tarn saw the turning and stopped his broom at the empty set-down and said nothing. Read the house’s arithmetic again --- bed under the roof, debt in the loft, a seventh year held back, the days to Kindling gone around as a closed fist --- and extended the file to the death-house bench and to the absent note. On Stone 8 was carried to the Fishstairs, where Mira flicked eel-bones, short-weighted Berr by two eels against two marks short, called the basket \emph{warm} off the slate and touched the grey cord when a figure was spoken; a collector’s cuff crossing the bridge brought two present-tense sentences of a hospital cafeteria and a wrapper eaten to the last crumb, and he counted four steps down, four, and a landing that was not a step. On Stone 9 was set in the bridge’s shade, where Dessa called the pits’ cough weather, counted nineteen into her thumb and put him among the bits without looking in, and where Mira put a brown-edged crust into the fold that he could smell but could not lift. Sella carried him home and said nothing; at dusk she banked the coals, counted her loaves twice and came back to the same place, and he lay with the crust warm at his side and his hand going up an inch and coming down --- four, four and a gap.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 6: Lived Days 10--14, Stone 16--20, ten to fourteen days old. On Stone 16 watched Tarn measure the kindling (four, four, a space where the fifth should be) and Sella move her lips along the loaves so the days to Kindling stood as a shape; Alda came at mid-morning, reached for her slate before him, touched the tin once, pressed the fold flat too long, crossed two fingers at the red edge of his wrist without knowing it, covered the sign with an unasked-for date and wrote a second note she turned writing-down into her shawl toward a floorboard he does not know. On Stone 17 Tarn went still for two breaths at \emph{you’ve done well}; a pot turned toward on the bench gave nothing and he filed a second interval beside the first, count still five from four sources; Sella named the kiln’s breath and Tarn told of the man in Mud End called merciful. On Stone 18 the number went around the yards as a fist; at the well a neighbour reached for her slate before her child and the hospital broke through in the present tense --- ceiling light at four, a chart with its note turned down, a hand going past it to a signature, a pocket holding wool where a lit phone with a name had lain --- and he looked at no name. On Stone 19 a man come up from the Ilm held ice with a dark hair running and stopping short of the edge; a woman from High Kiln said the thaw would come early and neighbours who wanted it late contradicted her; a neighbour back from the Court’s room described bench, pot, draught and gap and he kept the room in four separate places; Sella measured the ridge near two thumbs here and a finger thicker two doors down. On Stone 20, Account-day, Sella carried him down to the moot-post’s shade; the bell went four, four and a gap and nobody crossed himself; Berr read one in twelve, called the levy for the feast and said it was not called by him, went around the uncalled debt and did not look into the basket; at the Court’s table a soft-cuffed clerk laid his hand on the slate before the woman waiting and said it was entered as it stands, and the pause in the neat dark hand came a fourth time, unread and unjoined to the other three, with the Drawing collector’s hand with no pause kept apart. At dusk the coals were banked, the fold put right without a look at his face, and the cold crust left where it was put; the Five eleven days off, the household keeping the number badly and he keeping it exactly. Still mute, cracked, unranked, below Thin, carried, unable to read Grathic or lift a hand to his own chin.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 7: Lived Days 15--24, Stone 21--30, fifteen to twenty-four days old. On Stone 21 counted fuel and bread into the last tend in loaves, glances and a space, and heard a man come back from the ice with a number in a shut fist that he would not give; Sella touched the widow’s mark before the lid and at no other hour. On Stone 22 Tarn was sent for a collector for a neighbour and came back with a man whose fingertips were the colour of skimmed milk gone off and who said \emph{the measure is taken and the account stands as entered} to a slate; on the way back a carried vessel gave its flat note past the door, Tarn’s head turned a degree, and the boy filed it on the interval tray, count still five. On Stone 23 Jorra’s grey dust returned after five clean mornings and two records went hidden in one house; on Stone 24 Alda touched her tin unopened, crossed the sign at his wrist unaware, covered it with a date and turned a further note face-down toward a floorboard. On Stone 25 a pot cracked two paces from him with the flat knock and was called a pot gone wrong; he could not turn to place it and made a third interval, no sixth hearing. On Stone 26 the number for the Five went around three, two and whatever the moot gave out, and he kept one day after tonight. On Stone 27 ice-mice and the thaw argument were filed as weather; on Stone 28 Mira put a fresh crust beside the spent one, touched her grey cord and showed the second cord twisted twice, while Dessa coughed from the pits and called it weather. On Stone 29 the brooms came out and Sella measured Vail’s ridge by thumb against the death-house ridge; Garl’s coat kept its peg and the tiles’ debt was circled without a name. On Stone 30, Account-day and the year’s last market, Berr read one in twelve for the feast and said it was not called by him, the Five were three days off, and at the Court’s table the neat dark hand’s small stop came a fifth time and lay with the four unjoined; in one present-tense beat the flare light was orange on wet snow and a hand in a grey sleeve found wool where a lit phone with a name had lain, and he did not look. At dusk Sella set him on his bed under the roof, banked the coals and did not touch the mark; the fire kept four, four and a gap and Kindling was tomorrow. Still mute, cracked, unranked, below Thin, carried everywhere, unable to read Grathic or lift a hand to his own chin.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 8: Lived Days 25--30, Kindling through Ilmen 1, Y.H. 812--813, twenty-five to thirty days old. On Kindling watched the year’s fire come up the Clay Yard in a clay dish with a coal under ash, handed from hearth to hearth, and Sella tip it into the kiln after touching the widow’s mark before the opening and at no other hour; extended the count to its light --- four, four, and a place where a fifth would be if there were a fifth --- and heard the year’s first measure taken offstage with no figure spoken in the house. On Weighing heard a clean voice in a temple’s clothes read the measures, a whole return for a person not in the room and a name the household would not repeat, counted the silence after the name among the gaps, and set the Court’s room --- bench, pot, draught and a missing line heard through a doorway --- beside the birth room, the kiln-house and the death-house without writing a cause; Berr was glimpsed wiping his thumb, passing a finger over his slate and going off with his box locked. On the Long Night listened to stories of the Return with the fire out, filed the gap between question and answer, the left-out name and the stopped story with the intervals, kept the told bell’s four, four and a gap beside the heard bell in two places, and felt cold come at cheek, temple and wrist while neither breast nor crust was given. On the Remembering heard names pass along the yard and Garl’s name not spoken under the Vail roof, watched Alda lay dates where a name should stand, touch her tin once unopened and cross two fingers at the birth-flower without knowing it, and found wool in the pocket-place where a lit rectangle with a name had lain while the boat promise came in past tense, untagged; the charred slate lay untouched in the kiln ash. On the Last Day watched no third crust enter the fold, heard Mira answer a question with a question and her own answer and show the second cord twisted twice beneath the grey with the knots uncounted, and saw Sella measure both ridges with one thumb and leave the Ash where it lay. On Ilmen 1 watched the grey burned and called dealt with, found the coals still banked so the mark stayed untouched, heard Slate Row spoken of as a direction with one in twelve printed and unchallenged, and carried the count into Y.H. 813. Still cracked, mute, unranked, below Thin, carried everywhere; five hearings from four sources and no sixth, five pauses unjoined, nothing explained; his hand outside the wool went up an inch toward the warmth and came down.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 9: Lived Days 31–37, Ilmen 2–8, Y.H. 813, thirty-one to thirty-seven days old. At the yard well heard a woman say the water tasted different and a man say the ice was honeyed under the mud, and kept the shape of a change nobody would name (T085); watched Mira answer a question with a question, touch the grey cord under her apron when a figure was spoken and show the second cord twisted twice beneath it, knots uncounted (T025, T059). On Ilmen 3 watched Tarn set the small knife on its sill and announce it to the empty yard, six years counted and the seventh held back, Ash in his knuckles, wanting the late thaw that puts off the paying (T036). On Ilmen 4 watched Jorra come in from the back room with grey slate dust past the bent little finger and say nothing, filed dusty and clean forearms apart, and went around the space under the racks where whole slate should have stood (T035, T031). On Ilmen 5 watched Alda lay a date where a name should stand, touch the tin once unopened, make the two-finger sign at the birth-flower unaware, say \emph{warm and breathing} exactly and not true, and turn a fourth hidden note face-down toward a floorboard he cannot name (T007, T008, T023). On Ilmen 6 heard a pot set down out of a woman’s shadow answer nearly full --- a third sound, neither flat nor silent --- and filed it as the first earthly answer to the Stone 13 interval, advanced and not paid, while the flat hearings stayed five from four sources (T082, T061); watched Sella touch the widow’s mark before the opening and at no other hour (T079). On Ilmen 7 saw the hairline come up into the open ice of the Ilm and set it beside the missing Fishstairs step and the told bell in three places; watched Berr come back from the river with the red cord under his coat, wipe his thumb twice before touching nothing, keep a number he would not give and go off with the box locked; heard the Singing Sill note early and the well-roof argument end in weather (T083, T085, T041, T077). On Ilmen 8 stood at House Silt three doors down while Dessa coughed worse and still called it weather, got specific over four loaves and nineteen steps, smoothed the sieve-wire scar and did not look into the basket or say the number or the name; Mira passed her without looking and brought no crust; the Slip Brook ran clay-heavy a little high; and the shape of Dessa’s hand on the wicker reached in past tense, untagged, for a pocket-place and a lit rectangle with a name unlooked-at, the boat nine promises old on cold water (T008, T073, T044, T004). Carried up the yard at dusk under the Vail roof with the two crusts in the fold, no third, the carried fire under blind ash keeping four, four and a gap, his hand outside the wool up an inch toward the warmth and down. Still cracked, mute, unranked, below Thin; no power moved, no experiment, no joining.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 10: Lived Days 38–44, Ilmen 9–15, thirty-eight to forty-four days old, carried everywhere. Held on the bank at the Slip Brook while the yard lifted Dessa Silt out with their hands and no words; heard the small flat knock of a body cracked all the way through, the sixth hearing and second from a person, and filed it beside the five from four sources without joining or counting a seventh. Paid the held thumb-on-wicker detail in past tense, untagged: the grey sleeve, the small cold rectangle with a name not looked at, the boat nine promises old on cold water, the hand coming back with wool, nothing crossing. Watched Alda reach for her slate before the body and lay dates where a wonder should stand, watched the clerk at the Fishstairs set for a measure nobody had called, and filed the order of reaching apart from the other record-first hands. On Day 39 was set in the moot-post’s shade while one in twelve was read twice and the true subtraction went over the basket; kept four ways out of the square and the bell’s four, four and a gap. On Day 40 registered no collector coming for the woman in the brook and nobody naming the omission, kept the clean dark line left where it lay, and watched Tarn send his broom over the road to the Fishstairs without turning. On Day 41 saw Mira’s second cord twisted twice beneath the grey with neither knot counted, and no third crust; on Day 42 saw from the basket’s low angle the pewter tin above Dessa’s empty bed with its pale fold and thumb-rubbed lid, entering it nowhere. On Day 43 filed a green-mouthed woman looking at pots apart from Orra’s name, kept the Weir as a sixth like room with a weak board, and heard the Singing Sill early and called weather. On Day 44 heard Orra tie the forty-first knot and say \emph{forty} low into the basket and watched her watching him; he had no answer, kept the shape and the word on separate trays, and went home at dusk with both crusts still in the fold. Still cracked, mute, unranked, below Thin; no eighth hearing, no seventh pause, no power moved, nothing joined, paid or explained except a sound, a shape and a word.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 11: Days 45–47, Ilmen 16–18, forty-five to forty-seven days old. Carried below the north bridge at dawn and set out of the draught; watched a brine-gull go off upriver with a coal not yet cold and kept the subtraction nobody else kept, while the clerk at the Fishstairs put hand to slate before eye to stalls. Read the shape of Orra’s forty-first knot --- double turn, tail tucked, tied left over right, the weight of a thumb --- without its name; the word forty was not spoken again and Orra watched him watching. Watched Mira’s two cords shown with the knots uncounted and set on a board beside Orra’s without the boards touching. Under the roof watched the house’s arithmetic go on in loaves and glances and the widow’s mark touched once before an opening; watched Tarn’s knife announced and his broom sweep the collector’s road without turning, and Jorra’s bone-coloured forearms lead at the damper. On Day 46 watched Alda reach for the slate before the child, touch the tin unopened, cross the sign and cover it with a date, saying \emph{warm and breathing}, exact and not true. In the afternoon the barley smell stopped: the smoky crust was gone, and he set Sella’s, Alda’s and Mira’s hands on three places on a tray without making a cause. On Day 47 watched frost write on the well-lip, a number pass from fist to mouth to shoulder and arrive nowhere, Berr wipe his thumb twice and take himself out of his own sentence, a weir woman report the weak board, and the Singing Sill give its note early --- all called weather. Carried home at dusk with one crust in the fold and an empty place beside it. Still cracked, mute, unranked, below Thin; no power moved, no seventh hearing, no ending.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 12: Days 48–54, forty-eight to fifty-four days old, carried in the basket with one crust and an empty place in the fold. At the well frost-bloom wrote again on the lip, the oiled paper hung slack in its frame, and the two neighbours who had argued the ice fell silent; he filed the slack frame, the silence and the hairlines stopping short of the edge beside the honeyed ice and called no cause. On Account-day Berr read one in twelve over the basket and the true subtraction went unspoken while the bell went four, four and a gap. Jorra’s grey dust came back from the back room; Tarn’s head did not turn at a vessel’s note on Day 50 or at the nearly-full pot on Day 52, and the two ears kept their silence. Alda wrote a fifth note, touched the tin once unopened and covered the unaware sign with a date. A second pot answered nearly full and he filed it beside the first, advanced and not paid, with no hand to tap either. Mira’s two cords were shown side by side with knots uncounted and her board beside Orra’s not touching. More hairlines stopped short of the edge, the Singing Sill gave its note early, and the weak board at the Weir was said plainly still there and trodden by nobody. He carried the empty place through all seven days unnamed, kept six hearings beside and never among and the three hands on their tray, and his hand outside the wool went up an inch toward the warmth and came down.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 13: Lived Days 55--60, Ilmen 26--30 and Silt 1, fifty-five to sixty days old, two months at the close. At the yard well heard a man come downriver from Greybank tell how a counting room was shut in the last war and the men inside died of the breath with the damper closed, eighteen leagues east; the yard took it as history and nobody joined it to the kiln under his own roof, and he filed the saying on a tray of its own beside the told bell, the heard bell and the four-four-and-a-gap without writing a cause (T065). Carried three doors down to House Silt, saw the pewter tin above the empty bed with its pale fold and thumb-bright lid, and watched Alda lay the birth-slates writing-down before the fold, press it too long, cross the sign at the flower’s red edge unaware and cover it with a date, say \emph{warm and breathing} exactly and not true, touch her tin unopened and write no sixth note (T089, T007, T008). Kept the exact three days to Silt while the house kept them in loaves and glances, and watched the yard prepare a sweeping already done while Sella laid one thumb in the clean dark line and the same thumb in the death-house ridge without fetching a broom (T071, T013). At the last market watched Berr wipe his thumb twice and read one in twelve twice over the basket, the soft-cuffed clerk glimpsed hand-to-slate-before-eyes and silent, Mira answer a question with her own answer, touch her grey cord with the second twisted twice beneath it, show knots uncounted, keep her board beside Orra’s without touching it and bring no crust; a barrow of grey went out toward the Bone Orchard unread (T015, T090, T059, T013). On Silt 1 watched a new hairline of grey gather beside the clean dark line and Sella stand over it with a broom and call it thaw, and set the new grey and the left-in-place line on two places that did not touch (T092). Carried home at dusk with one crust in the fold and the empty place beside it unnamed, the river beginning to move under the ice, the six hearings still six and no seventh, his hand up an inch toward the new grey and down.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 14: Days 61–67. Carried everywhere at sixty-one through sixty-seven days old and kept the count exactly while nobody gave a figure; heard water going over water behind the racks and filed it as a fifth low thing, not a hearing; held six hearings, three near-full answers (a third filed on Silt 6), three intervals, the word, the knot’s shape and the weight of a thumb on separate trays and joined none; watched Sella keep her half-pace and touch the widow’s mark at no hour in seven days, Tarn announce his knife and check the cracked-pot place, Jorra bring dust out of the back room and move the damper ahead of her sentence; in House Silt saw the sixth note written and turned down and the pale stone gone, both unmentioned; heard Mira’s figure and cord and Berr’s twice-wiped thumb at the Fishstairs; on Silt 8 lay with one crust and the empty place, the honeyed ice and the current in veins, and his hand up an inch toward the water and down. Nothing joined, paid, explained or ended.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 15: Days 68–74, Silt 9–15, sixty-eight to seventy-four days old, carried at the half-pace through the flood. Heard the district’s note --- a low turning of many small failures inside one slow certain one, a vessel of enormous capacity with a thin place nobody would name --- under the four low sounds, and filed the coming and the going with no word and no cause. Below the sill read the child’s cold foot as the extremity going before the core, the afterdrop waiting on the far side of a warming he could not perform, and could not put a hand two paces out; the woman called it the cold, the yard called the water weather, and no cause or cure was spoken. On Account-day watched Berr wipe his thumb twice, read one in twelve over the standing water, take himself out of his own sentence and go off with the box locked; the true subtraction went over the basket and the number went from fist to mouth to shoulder and arrived nowhere. Watched the water go around the clean dark line at the Vail corner and the burned line two doors down, and Sella stand over both lines and the new finer grey with a broom and sweep neither while telling the fire it was the thaw. Saw Mira’s second cord twisted twice beneath the grey with neither knot counted, Orra standing at the flood’s edge with her board and cord and no answer, and Alda’s sixth page and the tin above the empty bed stay shut three doors down. Saw Tarn’s knife on its sill with the seventh nearly gone and his head not turning at a vessel’s note; saw Jorra’s grey dust on Silt 14 and his clean bone-coloured forearms on Silt 15, the damper moved ahead of Sella’s sentence and \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed. Kept six hearings, three near-full answers, three intervals, the word, the knot’s shape, the weight of a thumb, four low sounds and a fifth thing that was not a hearing on trays that did not touch; kept one crust in the fold with the empty place unnamed; crossed into Silt 16 with the count unspent. No experiment, no rank change, no recognition, no ending.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 16: Days 75–77, Silt 16–18, seventy-five to seventy-seven days old. At dusk carried up the yard at the half-pace, set on the bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, fold put right without a look at his face, thread frozen and unwiped, river note through the finger’s-width-open door and the fire’s four-four-and-a-gap through the floor kept apart. No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no experiment, no rank change, no new scar or possession. \item Ch 21: Days 101–103, Seed 12–14, one hundred and one to one hundred and three days old, three lived days with no recap. No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no power moved, no experiment, no rank change, no ending.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 24: Lived Days 110–112, Seed 21–23, one hundred and ten to one hundred and twelve days old, three lived days with no recap, the planting month in its last tend. \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 26: Days 116–119, Seed 27–30, the planting month going out and Reed coming on in the dark beyond the door. One hundred and sixteen, then seven, eight and nineteen days old — three months and twenty-six through twenty-nine days — and nobody saying so. On Seed 27 he was carried to the very edge of the worked strips and watched the last hands come out, counted in glances and handfuls and never in a figure: a woman lifting two chaffed fingers and shutting them, a man with a barrow shaping the number of backs with his mouth and thinking better of it. One hand that went in on Seed 15 did not come out with the rest; the yard went around the empty place with a look and no number, and he filed it on a place of its own as a chart closed with a neat line over a note nobody had opened (T098 planted, not paid, held for a later body or figure), not laid beside the shelf’s two gaps, the fold’s one crust and its empty place, or the word forty. On Seed 27 and again on Seed 29 neighbours laid two bare boards under one appetite in a single breath without seeing they had joined two rooms; he set each saying beside the earlier tellings and the watcher’s late turn, made no joining of his own, allowed no fourth likeness and no third gap. On Seed 28 he read the damper’s double bite once more as the iron that holds and the iron that takes, saw Jorra’s bent finger lead at it while Tarn’s stroke went on over the flagstones without the half-check and the stones kept the stopped place, and kept two silences unjoined and the loan uncalled; across the market a silent woman’s green at the mouth was filed beside Berr’s and the Silt 30 green, three shapes in three places with no name, no dialogue and no ear. On Seed 29 Mira’s second cord showed twisted twice with neither knot counted, Alda’s sixth page and both tins stayed shut, and the cold foot stayed dark inside three turns of wool below the sill. On Seed 30 Berr read one in twelve over the very absence nobody entered and took himself out of his own sentence with \emph{your house}, the heard bell stayed beside the told bell and the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the out-of-line landing. At the going of the light Sella carried him up from the moot-post’s shade at the half-pace, went around the space beneath the lowest rack, set him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without looking at his face and left the thread frozen and unwiped, her hand resting a half-beat longer than the setting needed; she told the fire it was the thaw, turned the coals with the back of a broken pot, said \emph{The house will keep it}, counted under her breath toward no opening, pushed a strand of coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist, the grey streak pale in the dying light, and did not look toward the bed. The river’s note came through the finger’s-width gap and the kiln’s four, four and a gap through the floor, and the two counts did not meet and the three counts did not become one. One hundred and nineteen stood unspent and spoken by nobody, and his hand outside the wool went up an inch toward the note of water over water and came down. Nothing was joined, named, paid or ended; no seventh hearing, no sixth sighting, no knot counted, no word forty, no tin or box opened, no name or body for the missing hand. No new scar, possession or change of voice; the surgeon’s register stayed inside his head and the old life stayed offstage.

\end{itemize}

\item Ch 31: Lived Days 132–134, Reed 13–15, Thirdday to Fifthday, one hundred and thirty-two through one hundred and thirty-four days old — four months and twelve through fourteen days — nobody saying so. \textbf{Day 132 (Reed 13):} at the Clay Yard and the reed beds watched the yard go around the clean dark line, the new finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with the broken birth-slates and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). At the close six hearings stood six beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced, four stoppings as objects and not a rule, one crust and no third, two shelf gaps in a room that does not touch, the word forty unspoken, Alda’s six pages and both tins and Dessa’s tin shut, the loan uncalled and the seventh year not given; three counts of river, fire and boards stayed in three places that did not become one. Old life offstage throughout: no present-tense break, no `**` tag, no power used, no rank change. Nothing joined, paid, named, opened, called or ended; forward.

\item Ch 34: Lived Days 141–143, Reed 22–24, Secondday to Fourthday, one hundred and forty-one, forty-two and forty-three days old, four months and twenty-one to twenty-three days, nobody saying so. \textbf{Day 141:} at the Clay Yard and reed beds the last bundles came up judged by the arm that carried them, a cutter told a girl with a creel her arm knew what went into a bundle and that was the whole of it, and a woman asking what the hands would be paid was answered with the weather and the river and shut two fingers out of a fist; the yard went around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the broken birth-slates and the place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T098 carried); a reed-cutter’s grey cord went past along the boards straightened and turned where no slate lay, its knots unread (T099 carried). \item Ch 35: Lived Days 144–146, Reed 25–27, one hundred and forty-four to one hundred and forty-six days old, carried at the half-pace from every open slate. On Day 144 read the last bundles of reed as a record in muscle, judged by the arm that carried them and never by a figure; a girl with a creel was told her arm knew what went into a bundle and that was the whole of it, and a man who asked what the hands would be paid was answered with the weather and the river. On Day 146 watched Alda lay her birth-slates before the fold three doors down, cross the flower unknowing, cover it with \emph{Stone seven. The account went up on the eighth, before the paper went out}, say \emph{Warm and breathing} exact and not true, touch her tin unopened and leave six pages turned toward a floorboard with both tins shut (T007/T008/T023/T089, not paid again). The old life stayed offstage: no present-tense break, no `**` tag, no departure from his eyes. No power moved, no rank change, no opening, no ending.

The household’s own keeping of Garl held through all three days — salt coat, hollow seat, clean dark line and finer grey unswept, proverb gone to the pot, uncalled debt against the tiles — none made a lesson of, no collector called (T009/T013/T092). Cost-questions went to the pot and the weather on all three days and away level, nothing priced, refused or entered (T077); the sweet edge of lead glaze came up off High Kiln on wrong winds and went out on them, a direction with no cause named, no second edge paid and no pot lost (T064 held). \textbf{The first advancement:} on the morning of Day 205 a voice came up from Slate Row, spoken over the boards and not to the basket, saying a slate had burned in the night — no owner, no room, no hand at the flame, no reason — and he filed it on a place of its own beside Jorra’s grey dust and the two shut-room tellings with a hand between them, a direction arriving nowhere, not a cause, not a third telling, not a hearing, not a payment, nothing a clerk could chart (T035/T031/T065/T095, advanced and not paid). Jorra grew quieter and \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed, the promise of the boy’s name ungiven. \textbf{The second advancement:} asked five times across the three days, the hand went up an inch and answered five ways; then in the small hours of Day 206, with Sella gone to her own bed and no count at her fire in the room that does not touch his to hold against, it went up toward the river’s note, stayed for the length of the river’s own low interval and came down on the river’s next low note — a coordination with the one rhythm through the door, filed on a sixth place, not a longer reach, stronger hand, hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, one of the three held changes, key, power or rule, no payer named (T061/T082 advanced, not paid). Six answers in three days, each exact, complete and worth nothing; he still cannot close two inches, lift the crust or speak a number. Two hundred and six stands exact, unspent and spoken by nobody; the river goes on over water without noticing the inch. No new scar, possession or change of voice.

\item Ch 52: Lived Days 207–209, Ember 28–30, Eighthday to Tenthday, two hundred and seven through two hundred and nine days old — six months and twenty-seven days to six months and twenty-nine days — nobody saying so. Three dated days, each lived in two scenes; the kiln breathing in fours with a gap, the carried fire’s fifth without a payer for 207, 208 and 209 days, the river’s note through the finger’s-width door and the boards’ four nails, four and a thumb-width knot — three counts in three places that do not become one (T088, T071/T072, T061/T082). Instruction to wool, fire, pot, broom, running water and river wind, never the basket; \emph{the house}, \emph{The house will keep it}, half-pace, jar-glance without a touch, pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with the half-beat and no look toward the bed, gruel from the house’s own dish with his mouth unwiped, lips along a two-gapped row with no figure, finger kept from beneath the charcoal, widow’s mark untouched since before the kiln on Ember 1 — no opening in twenty-nine days, the two rooms that do not touch (T058/T079, T100). Garl kept in objects at the very end of the kiln month — salt coat, hollow seat, unswept clean dark line and finer grey called the thaw, proverb gone to the pot, debt against the tiles uncalled and unnamed — no lesson made, no collector called, his name unspoken for two hundred and nine days (T009/T013/T092). Cost-questions to the pot and the weather, nothing priced, refused or entered; the sweet edge of lead glaze on a wrong wind taken as a direction, no cause named and no second edge paid (T077, T064 held). \textbf{The chapter’s one true change, advanced and not paid:} on Day 209 the third and last Account-day and last market of the kiln month was read over the basket: Berr came up short off the clay road with the red cord folded square under his coat and green glaze at one corner of his mouth, wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, held a narrow slate unopened to his forearm, passed a finger over the figure and read \emph{One in twelve, as the notice says} low into the top of the crowd, the figure going twice over the basket, once for the moot and once for the households that came late; he said \emph{The levy is called. It is not called by me} and \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, and went off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness. The district’s arithmetic changed for the third time and cannot be changed back; the printed figure stands unchallenged and a figure read aloud is still not the figure paid, answering nothing for the man carried out on Day 188 (T015/T041/T047/T077). The bell went four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, heard beside told; Hessa took the slate up the road unread, the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the out-of-line landing, the sixth green a colour and the foundling a shape with no seventh of either (T078, T080, T090, T050/T051, T033/T034 held). The burned-slate word came a second time, still a direction with no owner, room, hand or reason, no third telling and no cause (T035/T031/T065/T095). Tarn brought the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stopped, nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, the Seed 16 breath unspent; Jorra’s finger held in the cold damper until the sentence reached the pot, a remembered repetition (T036/T076, T062). \textbf{Second advancement, unpaid:} in the small hours of Day 209, with Sella gone to her bed and no breathing number anywhere in the house, the hand went up an inch toward the river’s note and came down at once against the fold — a miss under the very conditions that gave the one-rhythm holding on Day 206, and no failure in the miss. Filed on its sixth place, not a longer reach, hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, held change, key, power or rule, no payer named (T061/T082). He still cannot close two inches, lift the crust or speak a number. The file was exact, complete and worth nothing; Ember went out without a boundary drawn and neither month-name corrected, and the count went forward into Day 210 unspent. No new scar, possession, power or rank; the old life offstage.

\end{itemize}

\item Ch 53: Lived Days 210–212, Grain 1–3, Firstday to Thirdday, two hundred and ten through two hundred and twelve days old — six months and thirty days to six months and thirty-two days — nobody saying so. Instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom, the running water and the river wind and never the basket; \emph{the house}; half-pace; jar-glance without a touch; the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat at the setting and no look toward the bed; gruel from the house’s own dish with the mouth unwiped; lips along a two-gapped row with no figure; finger kept on top of the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stays unread; the widow’s mark untouched because no morning, shelf, rack, yard or dusk was an opening and there has been no opening in thirty, thirty-one and thirty-two days (T058/T079, T100). Garl kept in objects through the turning of the month — salt coat holding a broader man’s shape with the crease at the left shoulder, hollow seat with its leftward lean, clean dark line and finer grey called the thaw unswept, proverb gone to the pot, debt against the tiles circled without a name — no lesson made, no collector called, his name unspoken for two hundred and twelve days (T009/T013/T092). The yard went around the pan’s gone ring, the bare trough whose water was called weather, the broken birth-slates under the lowest rack, the field’s empty place and the place the carriers crossed with a look and a wide step and no number; no third gap came, no fourth likeness was made a cause and no finger of his was drawn across the absences (T098 held). Cost-questions went to the pot and the weather and arrived nowhere: a neighbour at the door on Days 210 and 212, a rack woman with slip dried pale in her wrists and a man who kept a number shut in his fist at the well on Day 211 (T077). Six hearings beside and never among with the sixth out of a person and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, told bell beside heard, told figure beside paid with Ember’s third reading still locked up the road, nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, three held changes on three places, the loft scrape on a fourth, the pale line on a fifth and the held inch on a sixth; the file laid out as instruments on a towel, exact, complete and worth nothing (T061/T082, T100, T060/T086/T097 held). \textbf{The hand was asked six times across the three days and answered as the body answers:} down before the counted breath finished (210 morning), held for the small intake only (210 small hours), down at once (211 morning), held for the river’s own low interval and down on the river’s next low note (211 small hours, the one-rhythm coordination remembered), held for the small intake only (212 morning), and in the small hours of Day 212 with Sella gone to her own bed and the two rooms not touching, up an inch toward the note of water over water, held through the small intake, the hold and the letting go of one of the breaths Sella counts at her fire and down with the breath — the old two-rhythm coordination remembered, not a change made again — filed on its sixth place beside the others and laid across nothing, no payer named and nothing standing up out of it as a longer reach, stronger hand, hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, held change, key, power or rule (T061/T082, advanced and not paid). He still could not close the two inches to the pot handle, lift his chin the two inches to the crust or speak a number anybody under any roof had been asked to believe. On Days 210, 211 and 212 Tarn told the wood \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, brought the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stopped with no figure and no name, drew the breath he should have spent and did not spend it, left nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the loan uncalled and no collector on the road (T036/T076). Jorra came through with meal-fine grey slate dust past the bent finger and under the nails, kept dusty and clean forearms on one tray, told a pot \emph{You’ll do}, withheld its note from a man on a wrong wind whose saying about a pot singing early stayed a saying, gave no name to the men who went low into the back room before first grey, kept the burned-slate word a direction arrived nowhere beside the dust and the two shut-room tellings with a hand between, and held his bent finger in the cold damper until Sella’s sentence reached the pot as a remembered repetition; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise of the boy’s name stayed ungiven (T035/T031/T062/T065/T095). \item Ch 64: Lived Days 243–245, Smoke 4–6, Fourthday to Sixthday, three dated days in six scenes, two hundred and forty-three through two hundred and forty-five days old — six months and sixty-three days to six months and sixty-five — nobody saying either figure under any roof (T071/T072). Smoke went on without a boundary drawn and neither district month-name was corrected; no market, Cross or bell in three days, Smoke 10 (Day 249) four mornings ahead at the close and unbrought. First smell hot clay under tallow, wet wool under that, sour Ash breath of the unswept corner called the thaw; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap, not a bell.
