\CRsheetheading{Chapter Log}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 1: Lay on the pallet through the birth and the night, face turned toward the wall where the room allowed it. Counted nineteen out and nineteen back until the count stopped and her pulse took it up. Rubbed the sieve-wire scar while deciding how much to say; got specific --- nineteen steps twice daily since Y.H. 806, four loaves baked in Grain, three to the levy and one eaten with her feet up, the seventh of Stone in eight hundred and twelve --- and would not name the child. Called him the little hot one and the flower. Pressed the wool flat at his shoulder with two fingers that stayed longer than the cloth required. Smiled the \emph{door shut} while Sella Vail’s hand hovered. Took Mira’s crust of Vail-smoked barley bread.

\item Ch 2: On Day 2 coughed from the pits, called it weather, rubbed the pale sieve-wire scar and got specific about steps, loaves and the day of the month; said a body can be warm and still be gone without looking at the child. On the third morning got up while Sella was at the bench, followed the covered bundle to the end of the Clay Yard and took none of the nineteen steps after it. Pulse in throat, thumb on scar, the door-shut smile; said nothing and did not say his name. Heard Alda say he had gone in the levy among the children taken for the account, asked only \emph{where}, and asked nothing further as the dates went on arriving. She believes him spent and will believe it three years.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 4: Day 6, dusk. Stood at the threshold of House Silt three doors down with her shoulder against the jamb as Sella carried the basket past. The cough came up out of the pits and she said \emph{weather}; her thumb went to the pale sieve-wire scar, the door-shut smile came down, and the nineteen steps went out of her feet and into her thumb, counted because the count kept a larger thing out of the room. She did not look into the basket. The boy’s mouth worked under the wool and Sella shifted the basket up against her hip and went on toward the bed. She does not know her son is in it and will not say the number or the name.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 5: Day 9, morning, at the edge of the fish-trade in the north bridge’s shade. Stood at the end of nineteen steps with her shoulder against nothing, slip-grey nails, wet clay dried at her hem and the pale sieve-wire scar up the inside of her left forearm. Coughed from the pits in a low short way and called it weather, then put the door-shut smile back on her face. Said \emph{nineteen out and nineteen back}, four loaves on the seventh of Stone in eight hundred and twelve, three to the levy and one eaten with her feet up, and bits to the woman who comes with a basket; smoothed the scar with her thumb. Counted the nineteenth into her thumb again and did not look into the basket, which held her son, and did not say the number or the name.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 7: Day 22, Stone 28, came to the yard mouth at the end of nineteen steps with slip-grey nails and wet clay dried at her hem, shoulder against the jamb; the cough came up out of the pits, she put her hand over her mouth and, when it had passed, said \emph{It’s the pits. Comes up in the cold. Weather} to the ground. Got specific because a truth had come near --- nineteen out and nineteen back, four loaves on the seventh of Stone in eight hundred and twelve, three to the levy and one eaten with her feet up, and bits to the woman who came with a basket. Her thumb went once over the pale sieve-wire scar and the door-shut smile came down; she did not look into the basket going past her shade. Has not said the number in three years and has not said the name in three years, and still believes him spent among the Forty. Mira passed with a fresh crust and did not look at her.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 9: Day 37, Ilmen 8, came to the yard mouth three doors down at the end of nineteen steps with slip-grey nails and wet clay dried at her hem, her shoulder against the jamb as if it held her up. The cough came up out of the pits in a low short way, she put her hand over her mouth and, when it passed, said \emph{It’s the pits. Comes up in the cold. Weather} to the ground; it was worse than Stone 28 and she called it the same thing. Because a truth had come near she got specific --- nineteen out and nineteen back, four loaves on the seventh of Stone in eight hundred and twelve, three to the levy and one eaten with her feet up, and bits to the woman who came with a basket --- laying the figures out small and separate so nothing larger could be fitted onto the bench. Her thumb went once over the pale sieve-wire scar up the inside of her left forearm and the door-shut smile came down; she said \emph{A body can be warm and still be gone. You learn that in the pits.} She did not look into the basket going past her shade and did not say the number or the name. Mira passed without looking at her and brought no crust, and the Slip Brook ran clay-heavy a little higher than it should behind the racks. Still alive at the close; the sixth hearing and the shape of her hand on the basket handle are held for Day 38.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 10: Day 38, Ilmen 9. Taken in the night by the clay-heavy rise of the Slip Brook from the end of nineteen steps, and dead from the opening of the scene; the yard lifted her out with their hands and no words, with silt in the creases beside her mouth and the clay set in her nails. The boy, thirty-eight days old, was held on the bank and could not move or look away; the small flat knock of her body cracked all the way through was the sixth hearing of the full note and the second from a person. The small quick grip of her thumb on the wicker handle, staying one breath and letting go, was paid in past tense and untagged and kept where things with no hour are kept; the hand in the grey sleeve went into a coat pocket for a small cold rectangle with a name unlooked-at and came back with wool. She did not say the number or the name and died believing him spent among the Forty; the number stayed in her thumb and the name under the sieve-wire scar and the lie told for mercy became a fact nobody could correct. No collector was called and nobody named the omission. On Ilmen 13 a clay jar that had gone over with milk was fetched from her room and set on a shelf under the Vail roof, and the pewter tin above the empty bed still held its scrap of birth-cloth, unopened.

\CRcharacter{Garl Vail}{the man whose warmth was left where it lay}{build/portraits/garl-vail.pdf}{\CRfield{Also called}{Garl, Garl of the Vail, the dead wheel-keeper, the uncollected}\CRfield{Role}{family}\CRfield{Born}{Y.H. 775, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath}\CRfield{Kind}{human (Grathic)}\CRfield{Origin}{Low Kiln, Sill, Grath; fourth generation of House Vail}\CRfield{Allegiance}{House Vail kiln-house; Kiln-Masters of Sill}\CRfield{Status}{dead (Stone, Y.H. 811; uncollected in the Long Cold; warmth lost to the Waste; his name unspoken under the Vail roof for 293 days at the close of Day 293, Frost 24, the tile debt neither paid nor settled nor done with and no collector up or down the clay road on Frost 22, 23 or 24; earlier: his name unspoken under the Vail roof for 290 days at the close of Day 290, Frost 21, the tile debt neither paid nor settled nor done with and no collector up or down the clay road on Frost 19, 20 or 21; earlier: his name unspoken under the Vail roof for 287 days at the close of Day 287, Frost 18, the tile debt neither paid nor settled nor done with and no collector up or down the clay road on Frost 16, 17 or 18; earlier: his name unspoken under the Vail roof for 281 days at the close of Day 281, Frost 12, the tile debt neither paid nor settled nor done with and no collector up or down the clay road on Frost 10, 11 or 12; earlier: his name unspoken under the Vail roof for 278 days at the close of Day 278, Frost 9, the tile debt neither paid nor settled nor done with and no collector up or down the clay road on Frost 7, 8 or 9; the first firing of Frost behind the household with no payment or lesson made of it; the stayed frost and the plate of ice lifted from the trough entered nowhere and no payer named to them)}\CRfield{First seen}{Chapter 2}}{\CRsheetheading{Appearance}
He is known in the house by objects rather than by memory. The wheel in the shed has a seat worn hollow on the left side where he sat for twenty years, and Sella will not let anyone fill it. A coat of his hangs on a peg behind the door with the salt stains still in it, and she has never taken it down, though Jorra has twice reached for it in the dark and stopped. He was a big man with clay in the creases of his hands and a laugh that ended in a cough; his left thumb was shaped by the wheel into a permanent hook. People who saw him said he moved slowly and arrived early, which in a kiln-house is the same thing. He smelled of wet clay and banked coals. In the house the absent smell is stronger than the memory: when the kiln is cold and the Ash ridge is thick, the room smells the way the corner of a room smells where something was left too long.

\CRsheetheading{Voice \& Manner}
He is remembered in proverbs, which means his voice has been improved by use and is probably not as good as the versions of it that survive. He never said a hard word in front of the fire — a habit Jorra has inherited without knowing it — and when he was angry he went to the wheel. His sayings are all about repair and none of them are about completion.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item “If it’s worth mending it’s worth mending twice. The second time is the real one.”

\item “Don’t tell me the pot’s ruined. Tell me what it was before it was ruined.”

\item “Feed the fire before you feed yourself. It’ll still be there in the morning. You won’t.”

\item “A man’s hands know what his head’s still arguing about.”

\item “Leave the crack showing. People trust a thing they can see has been handled.”

\end{itemize}

\CRsheetheading{History}
Fourth generation of Vails, born in the kiln-house and married to Sella, a slip-mixer’s daughter, in Y.H. 796. He kept the wheel for twenty years, threw the tiles that went into the floor of the Cross market, and was offered a price for his measure by a Sere factor in Y.H. 809 which he refused and did not mention for a year. He had two children: Jorra, born Y.H. 796, and Enna, born Y.H. 802, who died at nine months of the second chill and whose death he sat through without being able to do anything that mattered. In Y.H. 810 he began to be what Low Kiln calls walking thin — a vessel leaking faster than a man of his trade should leak — and he said nothing about it, because a kiln-master who admits a flaw loses the wheel.

In the Long Cold of Y.H. 811 the Ilm lay under ice for ninety-four days and no collector could cross from Greybank. Garl’s vessel gave in the first weeks of Stone. He died at home with Sella beside him and no iron tube in the room, and his warmth went where warmth goes when nobody takes it: into the Waste, unbanked, unrecorded, unreturned. In the morning there was grey Ash along the skirting board thicker than anyone had seen in that house. Tarn was sent to find a collector and turned back at the frozen ford. Jorra was thirteen and took the wheel a week later. The Vail household has been cool ever since, in a way that has nothing to do with the weather.

\CRsheetheading{Wounds \& Fears}
He knew he was leaking and kept throwing. That is the wound and it is also the answer to any question about why he is dead. He feared being banked thin and coming back as someone who would stand in his own house and not know the wheel; he feared more than that being spent whole and returned beautiful for somebody else’s benefit, which is what he had seen happen to a man he would not name. His contradiction: a man who mended pots for a living would not let anyone mend him, and called the refusal \emph{not wanting to be a bother}, which is the gentlest lie in the district and the most expensive.

\CRsheetheading{Desires}
He wanted to leave the wheel to Jorra whole, with the seat still worn and the note still true, and to come back as himself one day and teach the boy what a full note feels like under the knuckle. He thinks he wanted a whole return for himself. What he needed was to understand, before he died, that a vessel can be repaired without first being emptied — the thing his son’s household’s foundling will one day prove in the face of every priest in Sarn. He did not live long enough to be wrong about it in an interesting way, which is why his absence still has work to do.

\CRsheetheading{Bonds}
\textbf{Sella Vail} — his wife. She decided he would not be collected; he did not ask her to decide. A promise unkept gathers Ash in Sarn as surely as a debt, and the ridge in their room is the shape of theirs. \emph{Ch 2:} she touches the widow’s mark before the kiln and at no other time; she will not let anyone fill his seat or take his coat down, and the house keeps a private roll in which he is entered and which it does not show to a man from Slate Row. \emph{Ch 3:} the mark she touches only before the kiln was confirmed by the factor at Greybank and entered at the Court as a kindness, and she did not answer Berr when he said it; she went on covering the boy’s ears against the river wind instead.

\textbf{Jorra Vail} — his son, who has his hands and not his patience. Garl never told the boy he was proud of him. The boy has spent three years building a life around the absent sentence. \emph{Ch 2:} Jorra sits in the hollow seat he cannot fill and goes to the wheel when he is angry, which is the habit Garl had and never explained.

\textbf{Corin} — he never met the boy, who now sleeps under his roof and uses a warm stone that was warmed at Garl’s fire. There is a late recognition in this: the dead man’s hearth warmed the child he would take in, and a promise that cannot be settled because it was never made. \emph{Ch 2:} the boy read him as a man-shaped gap --- four, four and a space where the fifth thing should be --- and saw the charred edge of a slate in the kiln ash without knowing whose hand had written on it.

\textbf{Berr Clay, the Thane of Clay} — owed Garl for a consignment of tiles and never entered it. Garl never called it in. The Vail house has been short of coin ever since, and the debt has gathered interest in the Court’s books even though nobody in Low Kiln can read them. \emph{Ch 3:} at the Cross the debt was spoken around and never named, a space in Berr’s sentence with the shape of the hollow seat; his care not to call it was another kindness entered nowhere, for a debt uncalled can never be paid, settled or done with.

\textbf{Enna} — his daughter, who died at nine months and whose second chill he could not stop. He has been uncollected for a year; she has been returned thin or not returned at all, which nobody in the house will say aloud. Both are entered on the house’s private roll.

\textbf{Ch 4.} His coals held under ash all night and the kiln kept its four and four and a gap; the seat stayed hollow, the salt coat kept its shape, the ridge turned the corner unswept and the charred slate lay in the ash unexamined. Sella touched the mark for the kiln and not at the bank, said his sayings to the fire and the pot, and let the debt against the tiles lie uncalled while a measure was called in another house. Jorra came in with slate dust and did not say what the back room held.

\textbf{Ch 5.} The house keeps his shape without needing him in it. On Stone 13 the coals held under their ash and the kiln took its breath in fours and missed one; on Stone 15 the coat kept its salt-stiff shape on the peg, the seat its hollow on the left, and the ridge ran to the corner and turned it without a break, unswept. His proverbs went to the fire and the pot --- \emph{feed the fire before you feed yourself} and \emph{leave the crack showing} --- and never to a person. The debt against the tiles stayed uncalled while another measure was called elsewhere, and he was not asked to settle either.

\textbf{Ch 6.} On Stone 20 his debt against a firing of tiles was spoken around once more at the Cross, a place in Berr’s sentence shaped like the hollow of a wheel-seat, and Berr went around it the way a woman goes around Ash left in a corner; it remains neither paid nor settled nor done with. On Stone 19 Sella measured the ridge with her thumb --- near two thumbs at Vail, a finger more two doors down where the man gave under the tube --- and said leave it, it will be swept on the Last Day. His coat kept its salt shape on the peg, his seat its hollow on the left, the charred slate lay in the kiln ash unexamined, and the proverbs went to the fire and the pot: \emph{leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled.}

\textbf{Ch 7.} On Stone 29 the boy lay at the edge of the floor with the two crusts beside him while Sella laid her thumb into the Vail ridge and then walked two doors down and laid the same thumb into the death-house ridge; both turned their corners without a break and neither would be swept before the Last Day. Garl’s salt-stiff coat kept its shape on the peg, his wheel-seat its hollow on the left, and his proverb went to the pot and the fire and never to the basket: leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled. At the door the uncalled debt against the firing of tiles went around the talk the way a woman goes around a pot left on the floor in the dark --- a careful circle and no word for the thing circled. On Stone 30 Berr went around the debt as carefully as Sella went around Ash, set the printed figure down instead, and the coat, the seat, the ridge and the proverb kept the house in his shape through the year’s last market.

\textbf{Ch 8.} Through the Five he was absent and kept by objects: the salt-stiff coat on its peg, the wheel-seat hollow on the left, the proverb going to the fire and the pot and never to the basket. Under the Vail roof his name was not spoken on the Remembering; Sella went around it as around Ash left in a corner. The Ash ridge turned its corner without a break and was measured twice by one thumb --- near two thumbs at Vail, a finger’s width thicker two doors down --- and left where it lay on the Last Day; on Ilmen 1 it was burned in the morning and called dealt with by a neighbour, and the corner was a clean dark line. His uncalled debt against the tiles was still uncalled through the turn of the year, and the charred slate lay untouched in the kiln ash.

\textbf{Ch 9.} Through Days 31–37 his place in the house is a clean dark line where the Ash ridge had turned its corner for a year and two days, burned on Ilmen 1 and called dealt with by a neighbour with a pail of water while Sella stood over it with a broom and said nothing. The proverb still goes to the pot and the fire and never to the basket: leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled. The crack had been showing all year in a grey line along the wall and now the line is gone and the proverb goes on being said to the pot. The salt coat keeps its shape on the peg, the wheel-seat its hollow on the left, and the debt against the firing of tiles lies where it lay through another turning of the year, neither paid nor settled nor done with.

\textbf{Ch 10.} His place in the house is the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned its corner for a year and two days and was burned and called dealt with on Ilmen 1. On Ilmen 11 Sella laid her thumb in that line and then walked two doors down and laid the same thumb in the death-house ridge, a finger’s width wider, and came back without saying which was which and without fetching a broom for either; the line was left where it lay. His salt-stiff coat kept its shape on the peg behind the door, the wheel-seat its leftward hollow of twenty years, and the proverb went on being said to the pot and the fire and never to the basket: leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled. The carried fire he first kept still lay under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, missing one breath in every four, and the debt against the firing of tiles was neither paid nor settled nor done with when a woman went into the brook uncollected and no collector came for her either.

\textbf{Ch 11.} His place in the house is kept by the same objects on all three days: the salt-stiff coat on its peg behind the door, the wheel-seat hollow on the left that nobody fills, the charred slate in the kiln ash swept around and never picked up, and the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned its corner, which is not swept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. His proverbs go to the fire and the pot --- \emph{feed the fire before you feed yourself} and \emph{leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled} --- and never to the basket, the second still said to the pot after the crack was gone. The uncalled debt against the tiles is neither paid nor settled nor done with. The carried fire he first kept still lies under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, and on Day 45 a brine-gull carried off one of its coals, not yet cold, with no slate the poorer for the loss.

\textbf{Ch 12.} His absence kept the house through seven more days: the salt coat held its broader shape, the wheel-seat its hollow that nobody fills, the charred slate its place in the ash and the clean dark line its place on the wall, unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. His sayings went to the fire and the pot and never to the basket. The carried fire he first kept lay under blind ash and the back of a broken pot missing one breath in every four, and the debt against the tiles was neither paid nor settled while another woman lay sixteen mornings uncollected and nobody found a word for it.

\textbf{Ch 13.} His absence keeps the house through the approach to Silt. The salt-stiff coat holds a broader man’s shape on its peg behind the door, the wheel-seat in the shed keeps its twenty-year hollow on the left that nobody fills, the charred slate lies in the kiln ash, and the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned stays unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. His proverb goes to the pot and the fire and never to the basket --- \emph{leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled} --- and goes now to a pot with no crack in it, a saying about honest repairs said over a corner where the repair was rubbed out. The carried fire he first kept lies under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, warming the boards by degrees and missing one breath in every four; the coal the brine-gull took on Day 45 is fifteen days gone, entered in no slate and missed in no account. On Ilmen 29 Sella lays one thumb in the clean dark line and the same thumb in the ridge two doors down and fetches no broom; a barrow of grey goes out toward the Bone Orchard at the last market and nobody looks twice. On Silt 1 a new hairline of grey gathers in the corner beside the clean dark line and Sella stands over it with a broom and calls it thaw, and does not sweep. The debt against the firing of tiles is neither paid nor settled nor done with.

\textbf{Ch 14.} His absence keeps the house through seven days in which the river comes up and the yard calls it weather. The salt-stiff coat holds a broader man’s shape on its peg, the wheel-seat in the shed keeps its twenty-year hollow on the left that nobody fills, the charred slate lies in the kiln ash unexamined, and the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned its corner lies as it has always lain. Beside it a new hairline of grey has gathered, finer than the old line, and Sella stands over it with a broom and does not sweep because the house says it is the thaw; the boy sets the two lines in two places and does not let one become the other. His proverb about leaving the crack showing goes to a pot with no crack in it, said over a corner where the repair was rubbed out, and costs more now than it did when he was alive to say it. The carried fire he first kept lies under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, warming the boards by degrees and missing one breath in every four; the coal the gull took on Day 45 is twenty-two days gone, entered in no slate and missed in no account. The debt against the firing of tiles is neither paid nor settled nor done with, and no collector came up the road for the woman twenty-nine mornings dead.

\textbf{Ch 15.} His absence keeps the house through the flood and the going of it. The salt-stiff coat holds a broader man’s shape on its peg, the wheel-seat in the shed keeps its twenty-year hollow on the left that nobody fills, the charred slate lies in the kiln ash unexamined, and the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned its corner lies as it has always lain. The Ilm came up over the Fishstairs in a thin brown sheet and stood a hand’s breadth short of that line and of the burned line two doors down, and when it went off into mud neither line had been swept; the boy set the standing line, the water that went around it and the new finer grey beside it in three places that did not touch. His proverb about leaving the crack showing went to a pot with no crack in it over a corner where the repair had been rubbed out, a saying that has outlived the thing it was true about and costs more now there is nobody to say it in his own voice. The carried fire he first kept lay under blind ash and the back of a broken pot at four, four and a gap, with its payer unnamed and the coal the gull took twenty-nine days gone, entered in no slate. The debt against a firing of tiles lay where it lay, neither paid nor settled nor done with, and no collector came up the road for the woman thirty-six mornings dead.

\textbf{Ch 72 (bonds).} Present in objects only, a keeping and not a story: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg, the hollow wheel-seat, the proverb gone to a pot with no crack and said over a corner where the repair was rubbed out, and the debt against a firing of tiles circled without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and sixty-nine days and no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Smoke 28, 29 or 30. Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and the ear-sentence stopped short of the calling word on all three days as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end. The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed for two hundred and sixty-nine days. No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 73 (bonds).} Present in objects only, a keeping and not a story: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg, the hollow wheel-seat, the proverb gone to a pot with no crack and said over a corner where the repair was rubbed out, and the debt against a firing of tiles circled without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and seventy-two days and no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Frost 1, 2 or 3. Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and the ear-sentence stopped short of the calling word on all three days as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end. The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand at four, four and a gap on Frost 1–3, its payer unnamed for two hundred and seventy-two days; Sella’s opening at the kiln mouth on the 2nd held the widow’s mark one breath and made no payment to any of it and no lesson of four openings in four months. The boy kept the finding that the household’s not-doings and his own kept gaps do not join for want of a payer, and did not lay it across this absence or any other. No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 74 (bonds).} Present in objects only, a keeping and not a story: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg, the hollow wheel-seat no one may fill, the proverb gone to a pot and the fire and never to a person, and the uncalled tile debt circling without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with and worse for being uncalled. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and seventy-five days and no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Frost 4, 5 or 6. Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and brought the ear-sentence to the calling word on all three days and stopped there as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end. The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed two hundred and seventy-three through two hundred and seventy-five days; the first firing of Frost was Sella’s work at the kiln mouth on the 2nd and paid nothing here and made no lesson of four openings in four months. The boy kept the finding that the household’s not-doings and his own kept gaps do not join for want of a payer, and did not lay it across this absence or any other. No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item \textbf{Ch 78 (bonds).} With Sella the house kept its shape around a man not in it: the coat on its peg, the hollow seat, the unswept line, the proverb said to the pot and the fire, the debt against the tiles neither paid nor settled. Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford, and brought the ear-sentence to the calling word and stopped on all three mornings with no tenth. Jorra gave the men in the back room no name and kept \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed. With the boy nothing was joined: the hundred and fiftieth answer stayed an object and not a doctrine, and the household’s not-doings stayed on a place apart from his own gaps for want of a payer. No bond changed hands, no name spoken, no collector on the clay road.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item \textbf{Ch 80 (bonds).} With Sella the house kept its shape around a man not in it: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg, the wheel-seat keeping its twenty-year lean and its hollow nobody fills, the clean dark line at the Vail corner with the finer grey called the thaw beside it, unswept both, the proverb said to the pot and the fire and never to a person, and the debt against a firing of tiles neither paid nor settled nor done with and worse for being uncalled. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and ninety-one through two hundred and ninety-three days; no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Frost 22, 23 or 24 (T009/T013/T092). Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and brought the ear-sentence to the calling word on all three days, stopping there as a remembered \textbf{ninth} stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven (T036/T076). The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed two hundred and ninety-one through two hundred and ninety-three days (T088); Sella’s opening before the kiln on Frost 2 held the mark one breath and paid nothing here and made no lesson of four openings in four months (T058/T079). Frost’s first and second arithmetics stayed locked in Berr’s box up the clay road with the printed one in twelve unchallenged and the figure read still not the figure paid (T015/T041/T047). The stayed frost on the well lip, the skinned trough and the plate of ice on its flat stone were called weather and entered nowhere, and no figure was taken off any of them (T083/T085 held). The Frost 14 saying gained a third shaping on Frost 23 from an ownerless voice over the boards and the well-roof, the slate-runner once carrying a name the district spent and not saying whose; three shapings were filed on a place of its own with a finger between every pair, not a witness, not a cause, not a confession, not a joining and not paid, and not joined to this absence (T080 advanced, not paid). The boy kept the hundred and sixty-second answer as an object and not a doctrine. No bond changed hands, no name spoken, no collector on the clay road, no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

\item \textbf{Ch 79 (bonds).} With Sella the house kept its shape around a man not in it: the salt-stiff coat with its left-shoulder crease on its peg, the wheel-seat keeping its twenty-year lean and hollow nobody fills, the clean dark line with its finer grey thaw unswept, the proverb said to the pot and the fire, the debt against the tiles neither paid nor settled nor done with and worse for being uncalled. Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford, and stopped the ear-sentence at the calling word on all three mornings with no tenth; Jorra gave the men in the back room no name and kept \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed. With the boy nothing was joined: the hundred and fifty-sixth answer stayed an object and not a doctrine, the twice-read figure stayed two accounts and not one, and the household’s not-doings stayed on a place apart from his own gaps for want of a payer. The Frost 14 saying’s second shaping was kept on a place of its own, not joined to this absence. No bond changed hands, no name spoken, no collector on the clay road, no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

\CRsheetheading{Arc So Far}
\textbf{Ch 80.} He stays dead and stays left: the house’s uncollected debt and the flaw in the floor nobody patches. The last working week changes nothing here; the carried fire he first kept still misses its fifth with its payer unnamed for two hundred and ninety-one through two hundred and ninety-three days, Sella’s opening before the kiln on Frost 2 paid nothing and made no lesson of four openings in four months, and the stayed frost, the skinned trough and the plate of ice remain yard weather entered nowhere with no payer named to any. Frost’s first and second arithmetics go up the road in Berr’s locked box alongside one another and pay nothing to this absence; the Frost 14 saying now stands at three shapings on a place of its own, the third from an ownerless voice on Frost 23 saying the slate-runner once carried a name the district spent and did not say whose, not joined to the hollow seat or the unswept line and not paid. The boy keeps the hundred and sixty-second answer as an object and not a doctrine. No collector comes up the clay road on Frost 22, 23 or 24 and his name is not spoken under the roof in two hundred and ninety-three days.

\textbf{Ch 79.} He stays dead and stays left: the house’s uncollected debt and the flaw in the floor nobody patches. The fourth working week changes nothing here; the carried fire he first kept still misses its fifth with its payer unnamed for two hundred and eighty-eight through two hundred and ninety days, Sella’s opening before the kiln on Frost 2 paid nothing and made no lesson of four openings in four months, and the stayed frost, the skinned trough and the plate of ice remain yard weather entered nowhere with no payer named to any. Frost’s second arithmetic goes up the road in Berr’s locked box alongside the first and pays nothing to this absence; the Frost 14 saying now stands at one saying and one second shaping on a place of its own, not joined to the hollow seat or the unswept line. The boy keeps the hundred and fifty-sixth answer as an object and not a doctrine. No collector comes up the clay road on Frost 19, 20 or 21 and his name is not spoken under the roof in two hundred and ninety days.

\textbf{Ch 78.} He stays dead and stays left: the house’s uncollected debt and the flaw in the floor nobody patches. The third working week changes nothing here; the carried fire he first kept still misses its fifth with its payer unnamed for two hundred and eighty-five through two hundred and eighty-seven days, Sella’s opening before the kiln on Frost 2 paid nothing and made no lesson of four openings in four months, and the stayed frost, the skinned trough and the plate of ice remain yard weather entered nowhere with no payer named to any. Frost’s first arithmetic stays locked in Berr’s box up the road; the Frost 14 saying about the runner holds with no second shaping and is kept on a place of its own, not joined to this absence. The boy keeps the hundred and fiftieth answer as an object and not a doctrine. No collector comes up the clay road on Frost 16, 17 or 18 and his name is not spoken under the roof in two hundred and eighty-seven days.

\textbf{Ch 73.} He stays dead and stays left: the house’s uncollected debt and the flaw in the floor nobody patches. The first firing of Frost goes ahead of him on Frost 2 with Sella’s hand to the widow’s mark and the carried fire still missing its fifth, and nothing about the firing pays, settles, names or mends the debt against the tiles; the boy keeps four openings as four and not a rule and does not lay the finding across this absence or any other. No collector comes up the clay road on Frost 1, 2 or 3 and his name is not spoken under the roof in two hundred and seventy-two days.

\textbf{Ch 72.} He stays dead and stays left: the house’s uncollected debt and the flaw in the floor nobody patches. Smoke’s third reading goes up the road in Berr’s box and does not reach him; the boy keeps the finding that three readings are three and not one account on a place of its own and does not lay it across this absence or any other.

He is an absence with objects attached, and in Chapter 2 the objects are given a room. The kiln breathes in fours with a gap where the fifth breath should be; the wheel-seat is worn hollow on the left by twenty years of leaning; a salt-stiff coat keeps a broader man’s shape on its peg behind the door; the Ash ridge runs the length of the skirting board and turns the corner without a break, near two thumbs wide, and nobody sweeps it before the Last Day. His sayings have outlived him and improved in the keeping, and the house says them to the pot and the fire and never to a person. In the kiln ash lies the charred edge of a slate with the writing gone off the end, swept around for a year and never picked up. In Chapter 3 the absence leaves the house and goes into the market: the kiln’s breath missed one as the boy was carried out, the uncalled debt against the tiles hangs in the space between Berr and Sella, and a barrow of the same grey Ash goes out through the north gate while nobody looks twice. The reader knows him by what the household and the district do around the hole before anyone says how the hole was made.

On Days 5 and 6 the absence keeps the house. The coals under their ash hold all night and the kiln goes on taking its breath in fours and a gap; the seat stays hollow on the left, the salt coat keeps its broad shape on its peg, and the Ash ridge along the skirting board is not swept. In the kiln ash the charred edge of a slate lies black on one side and eaten into the shape of a strip of bark, with the writing gone off the end, and nobody picks it up. His proverbs are said to the pot and the fire in his improved voice --- \emph{feed the fire before you feed yourself}, \emph{leave the crack showing} --- and never to a person. The debt against the tiles lies uncalled beside a measure that was called and entered, and the boy files the two facts together without joining them.

On Days 7, 8 and 9 the absence keeps the house as exactly as it did on Days 5 and 6: banked coals holding under ash, a breath missed in the fours, the coat, the seat and the unswept ridge, and the sayings improved by twenty years of use said to the clay and the fire. The boy now files the death-house bench and the interval of a note that did not come beside the older objects, and the uncalled debt beside the warmth entered nowhere, joining none of them. Garl stays dead; the house’s debt and the Ash ridge are the shape of the promise he never made and Sella never released.

On Days 10 through 14 the absence keeps the house as exactly as ever and acquires a measure: Sella lays a thumb in the grey and calls it near two thumbs here, a finger more two doors down, and says neither will be swept before the Last Day; Tarn offers to check the width. The coat keeps its salt shape, the seat its hollow, the charred slate lies in the kiln ash unexamined, and the sayings go to the pot and the fire and never to a person. At the Cross on Stone 20 the debt against the tiles is spoken around again, a space in a sentence shaped like the hollow seat, and Berr sets the printed figure down where everyone can see it instead. The boy puts the debt on the tray beside the fourth pause and joins neither to the other. Garl stays dead; the house’s debt and the Ash ridge remain the shape of a promise nobody made and nobody released.

On Days 15 through 24 the absence keeps the house through the last tend of the year and into its last market. The kiln takes its breath in fours and misses one on all ten days; the coat holds its salt shape, the seat its hollow, the ridge its unbroken corner and the charred slate its place in the kiln ash. The debt against the tiles is circled at the door on Stone 29 and gone around at the Cross on Stone 30, neither paid nor settled nor done with. On Stone 29 Sella measures the ridge by thumb against the death-house ridge, near two thumbs here and a finger thicker there, and a woman at the tubs says the grey will be left where it lies until the Last Day and burned the next morning and called dealt with. The boy puts the thumb-measured ridge on the tray beside the charred slate, the barrow of grey, the fourth and fifth pauses and the date said aloud, and does not join any of them. Garl stays dead; the house keeps its shape around a man who is not in it, and the debt goes on living by nobody saying the word for it.

On Days 25 through 30 the absence keeps the house through the Five and crosses the turn of the year. The coat keeps its salt shape on the peg, the seat its hollow on the left and the proverb goes to the fire and the pot and never to the basket; under the Vail roof his name is not spoken on the Remembering and Sella goes around it as around Ash left in a corner. The ridge turns its corner without a break and is measured twice by one thumb, near two thumbs here and a finger’s width thicker two doors down, and left where it lies through the baking; on the morning of Ilmen 1 it is burned and called dealt with by a neighbour, and the boy keeps the left-in-place ridge and the burned-and-called-gone ridge under the same hand. The coat, the hollow seat and the uncalled debt against the tiles survive the burning and the opening of the slates, and the charred slate lies untouched in the kiln ash. Garl stays dead; the house keeps its shape around a man who is not in it.

On Days 31 through 37 the absence keeps the house through the first warm days of the new year. The ridge’s place is a clean dark line and is not swept; the coat, the hollow seat and the charred slate in the kiln ash keep their places; the proverb goes to the fire and the pot and never to the basket, and goes on being said after the thing it was said about has disappeared. The carried fire from Kindling still lies under blind ash and a broken pot, warming the boards by degrees and missing one breath in every four, and the debt against the tiles is neither paid nor settled nor done with. Garl stays dead; the house keeps its shape around a man who is not in it.

On Days 38 through 44 his absence keeps the house as the first left thing the boy can set beside the second. On Ilmen 9, the morning a woman was taken out of the clay-heavy brook and nobody called it anything, his salt-stiff coat kept its shape on the peg behind the door, the wheel-seat its leftward hollow of twenty years, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash, and his proverb went to the pot and not to the basket. On Ilmen 11 Sella laid one thumb in the clean dark line where his Ash ridge had turned its corner and another in the ridge two doors down, and brought the knowledge back without a word and without a broom. The carried fire under blind ash missed one breath in every four; the uncalled debt against the firing of tiles lay where it lay through the Fish Blessing upriver; and the line where the ridge had been was not swept, because a line left where it is is still a line kept. Another woman had now been left where she fell, and the house went around both absences without giving either a name.

On Days 45 through 47 the absence keeps the house as the first left thing set beside a second. On the morning after the blessing a coal goes upriver with a brine-gull out of the fire the house keeps, and one warmth less is abroad with no account showing it; the boy keeps the subtraction and no one else does. Under the roof the coat keeps its broader shape, the seat its twenty-year lean, the charred slate its place in the ash and the clean dark line its place on the wall, unswept. The proverbs go to the pot and the fire and never to the basket, and the debt against the firing of tiles stays neither paid nor settled nor done with. Another woman has now been left where she fell for nine mornings and nobody has found a word for it; the house goes around both absences without giving either a name.

On Days 48 through 54 the absence keeps the house as the first left thing set beside a second. The salt-stiff coat holds a broader man’s shape on its peg, the wheel-seat its twenty-year lean that nobody fills, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash, and the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned its corner is not swept, because a line left where it is is still a line kept. His proverbs go to the fire and the pot and never to the basket. The carried fire he first kept lies under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, warming the boards by degrees and missing one breath in every four, and the coal the brine-gull took on Day 45 is entered in no slate and missed in no account. The uncalled debt against the firing of tiles is neither paid nor settled nor done with, while another woman lies sixteen mornings uncollected and nobody has found a word for it.

On Days 55 through 60 the absence keeps the house as the first left thing set beside a second and a third. The salt-stiff coat holds a broader man’s shape on its peg, the wheel-seat its twenty-year lean that nobody fills, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash and the clean dark line its place on the wall, unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. His proverbs go to the pot and the fire and never to the basket, \emph{leave the crack showing} still said over a pot with no crack in it and a corner where the repair has been rubbed out; the joke has outlived the thing it was true about and costs more now that he is not here to say it. The carried fire he first kept lies under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, warming the boards by degrees and missing one breath in every four; the coal the brine-gull took on Day 45 is fifteen days gone and entered in no slate. On Ilmen 29 Sella lays one thumb in the clean dark line and the same thumb in the ridge two doors down and fetches no broom, while the yard prepares a sweeping already done; at the last market a barrow of grey goes out toward the Bone Orchard and nobody looks twice. On Silt 1 a new hairline of grey gathers beside the clean dark line and Sella will not sweep it because it is the thaw. The uncalled debt against the tiles stays neither paid nor settled, while another woman lies twenty-two mornings uncollected and nobody has found a word for it.

On Days 61 through 67 the absence keeps the house as the first left thing set beside a second and a third. The salt coat holds its broader shape on the peg, the hollow seat its twenty-year lean that nobody fills, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash, and the clean dark line its place on the wall, unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. A new, finer line of grey gathers beside it on Silt 2 and stays there through the week, unswept because the house says it is the thaw and it will go when it goes; the boy sets the new line and the old one in two places and keeps them apart. His sayings go to the pot and the fire and never to the basket, \emph{leave the crack showing} still said over a corner where the repair has been rubbed out and a pot with no crack in it, a saying that has outlived the thing it was true about. The carried fire he first kept still lies under blind ash and broken pot at four, four and a gap, with its payer unnamed and the coal the gull took twenty-two days gone. The uncalled debt against the tiles is neither paid nor settled, while another woman lies twenty-nine mornings uncollected and nobody has found a word for it. The house keeps its shape around a man who is not in it.

On Days 68 through 74 the absence keeps the house through the flood and the going of it as the first left thing set beside a second and a third. The salt-stiff coat holds a broader man’s shape on its peg, the wheel-seat its twenty-year hollow that nobody fills, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash and the clean dark line its place on the wall, unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. The Ilm comes up over the Fishstairs and stands a hand’s breadth short of that line and of the burned line two doors down, and when it goes off into mud neither has been swept; the boy sets the standing line, the water that went around it and the new finer grey beside it in three places that do not touch. His proverb goes to a pot with no crack in it over a corner where the repair was rubbed out, a saying that has outlived the thing it was true about and costs more now there is nobody to say it in his own voice. The carried fire he first kept lies under blind ash and the back of a broken pot at four, four and a gap, its payer unnamed and the coal the gull took twenty-nine days gone; the debt against a firing of tiles lies where it lay, neither paid nor settled nor done with, while another woman lies thirty-six mornings uncollected and nobody has found a word for it.

Through Smoke 22–24, Days 261–263, the absence keeps the house as the first left thing and the debt that is kept by being left alone. The salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease holds a broader man’s shape on its peg behind the door, the wheel-seat keeps its hollow on the left that nobody fills, the proverb has gone to a pot with no crack and is said in the house’s voice to the fire and never to a person, and the debt against a firing of tiles is circled without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and sixty-three days, and no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Smoke 22, 23 or 24. Tarn keeps the unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and brings the sentence about an ear worth more than the debt to the calling word and stops there as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end. The carried fire he first kept answers four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed for two hundred and sixty-three days, and the boy files the house’s not-doings --- the loan uncalled among them --- as a finding with no payer, held apart from his own kept gaps with a finger between and not joined to Garl’s absence or any other absence (T009/T013/T092, T088, T061/T082). A keeping and not a story; nothing paid, settled, named or ended.

Through Smoke 25–27, Days 264–266, the absence keeps the house as the first left thing and the debt that is kept by being left alone. The salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease holds a broader man’s shape on its peg behind the door, the wheel-seat keeps its hollow on the left that nobody fills, the proverb has gone to a pot with no crack and is said over a corner where the repair was rubbed out, and the debt against a firing of tiles is circled without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and sixty-six days and no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Smoke 25, 26 or 27. Tarn keeps the unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the lip of its sill with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and brings the ear-sentence to the calling word and stops there as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end. The carried fire he first kept answers four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed for two hundred and sixty-six days; the boy keeps the house’s not-doings — the uncalled loan among them — as a finding with no payer, held apart from his own gaps with a finger between and joined to no absence (T009/T013/T092, T088, T061/T082). A keeping and not a story; nothing paid, settled, named or ended.

\textbf{Ch 74.} He stays dead and stays left: the house’s uncollected debt and the flaw in the floor nobody patches. The week of going around changes nothing here; the carried fire he first kept still misses its fifth with its payer unnamed for two hundred and seventy-five days, Sella’s opening before the kiln on Frost 2 paid nothing and made no lesson of four openings in four months, and the boy kept the household’s not-doings on a place apart from his own gaps for want of a payer. No collector comes up the clay road on Frost 4, 5 or 6 and his name is not spoken under the roof in two hundred and seventy-five days.

\textbf{Ch 75.} He stays dead and stays left: the house’s uncollected debt and the flaw in the floor nobody patches. \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 1: Does not appear; his name, the stone warmed at his hearth and the house’s silence around him are held for Chapter 2.

\item Ch 2: Present throughout Days 2 and 3 as the shape of the house. The kiln’s breath he kept alive was counted in fours and a gap; his seat stayed hollow, his coat stayed on its peg, his Ash ridge grew, and his proverb \emph{leave the crack showing} was said in the house’s voice to the pot and the fire. The house’s private roll was spoken around: he was entered on it, and the foundling’s name would be entered there in a careful hand. The charred edge of a slate lay in the kiln ash and was not examined. No collector was called.

\item Ch 3: Day 4, Account-day. Present as what is left where it lay. The kiln took one breath behind the boy as he was carried out and missed the next; the lead on Berr’s breath and the red cord folded square came with the confirmation of Sella’s widow’s mark, and the debt Garl left against the tiles went spoken around, neither called nor settled. In the afternoon a barrow of grey Ash went out through the north gate toward the Bone Orchard, the same work that went out every market-day; the boy put it with the ridge under the Vail skirting board and the charred slate in the kiln ash, and nobody explained any of the three.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 4: Days 5 and 6. Present as the shape of the house and its rule. The banked coals held under their ash through the night and the kiln breathed four, four and a gap; the hollow seat stayed unfilled, the salt-stiff coat stayed on its peg, and the Ash ridge ran to the corner and turned it without a break, unswept. The charred edge of the slate lay in the kiln ash and was not examined. His sayings went to the fire and the pot --- \emph{feed the fire before you feed yourself} and \emph{leave the crack showing} --- and nobody said them to the boy. The debt against the tiles lay uncalled while the year’s first measure was called and entered in another house, and the boy kept the two facts side by side.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 5: Days 7--9. Present as the house’s shape and its rule. The coals held under ash through the night and the kiln took its breath in fours and a gap; the salt-stiff coat kept its shape on the peg behind the door, the wheel-seat its hollow on the left, and the Ash ridge ran to the corner and turned it without a break, unswept and not to be swept before the Last Day. His sayings went to the fire and the pot --- \emph{feed the fire before you feed yourself} and \emph{leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled} --- and never to a person. The debt against the tiles stayed uncalled while a number of days to Kindling went around the house as a closed fist.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 6: Days 10--14. Present as the house’s shape and its rule. His coat kept its salt-stiff shape on the peg, his wheel-seat its hollow of twenty years on the left, the charred slate lay in the kiln ash unexamined, and his sayings went to the pot and the fire --- \emph{leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled} --- and never to a person. The kiln took its breath in fours and missed one on all five days. On Stone 19 Sella measured the ridge with her thumb, near two thumbs here and a finger more two doors down, and Tarn offered to check it; she said leave it, it’ll be swept on the Last Day. On Stone 20, Account-day, the debt against the firing of tiles was spoken around at the Cross and never named, a space in Berr’s sentence shaped like the hollow seat, and Berr went around it and set the printed figure down instead. Neither paid nor settled nor done with.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 7: Days 15--24. Present as the house’s shape and its rule on all ten days: the kiln breathing four, four and a gap; the salt-stiff coat on its peg behind the door, the wheel-seat hollow on the left, the Ash ridge running to the corner and turning it without a break and not to be swept before the Last Day, the charred slate lying in the kiln ash unexamined. His proverbs went to the pot and the fire --- \emph{feed the fire before you feed yourself}, \emph{leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled} --- and never to a person. On Stone 29 Sella laid her thumb in the Vail ridge and then in the death-house ridge, a finger thicker, and came back without saying which was which; the uncalled debt against the tiles went around the door talk in a careful circle with no word for the thing circled, and a woman at the tubs said the grey would be left until the Last Day, burned next morning and called dealt with. On Stone 30 Berr went around the debt at the Cross without naming it and set the printed figure down instead. Neither paid nor settled nor done with.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 8: Days 25--30. Present as the house’s shape and its rule on all six days: the salt-stiff coat on its peg behind the door, the wheel-seat hollow on the left, and the proverb going to the fire and the pot and never to the basket. His name was not spoken under the Vail roof on the Remembering and Sella went around it as around Ash in a corner. The ridge turned its corner without a break, was measured by one thumb at Vail and a finger’s width thicker two doors down on the Last Day, and was left where it lay through the baking; on Ilmen 1 it was burned in the morning and called dealt with by a neighbour, and the corner was a clean dark line. The uncalled debt against the tiles stayed uncalled through the turn of the year and the charred slate lay untouched in the kiln ash.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 9: Days 31–37. Present as the shape of the house and its rule. The place where the Ash ridge had turned its corner for a year and two days was a clean dark line, burned on Ilmen 1 and called dealt with by a neighbour with a pail of water while Sella stood over it with a broom and said nothing; it was not swept. His salt-stiff coat kept its shape on the peg behind the door and the wheel-seat its leftward hollow of twenty years and nobody filled it. The proverb went to the pot and the fire and never to the basket --- leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled --- and went on being said after the grey line along the wall was gone. The debt against the firing of tiles lay where it lay through another turning of the year, neither paid nor settled nor done with, and the charred slate lay untouched in the kiln ash. The carried fire under blind ash missed one breath in every four.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 10: Days 38–44. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing. On Ilmen 9, the day Dessa Silt was lifted out of the brook and no collector came, his salt-stiff coat held its shape on the peg behind the door, the wheel-seat its leftward hollow of twenty years, the charred slate lay untouched in the kiln ash, and the proverb went to the fire and the pot and never to the basket: leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled. On Ilmen 11 Sella measured the clean dark line where his Ash ridge had turned with one thumb and the ridge two doors down with the same thumb, a finger’s width wider, and left both where they lay. The carried fire under blind ash missed one breath in every four, and the debt against the firing of tiles stayed neither paid nor settled nor done with.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 11: Days 45–47. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing. On Day 45 a brine-gull took a coal not yet cold out of the carried fire he first kept, and one warmth less went out of the world with no slate the poorer; the boy kept the subtraction. The salt-stiff coat held its shape on the peg, the wheel-seat its hollow of twenty years, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash, and the clean dark line where the ridge had turned was not swept, because a line left where it is is still a line kept. The proverbs went to the pot and the fire and never to the basket, \emph{leave the crack showing} still being said after the crack was gone. The uncalled debt against the tiles was neither paid nor settled nor done with while no collector came for the woman the brook took nine mornings ago.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 12: Days 48–54. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing. On all seven days the salt-stiff coat held a broader man’s shape on its peg, the hollow seat its twenty-year lean, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash and the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned was not swept, because a line left where it is is still a line kept. His proverbs went to the pot and the fire and never to the basket; the carried fire he first kept lay under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, warming the boards by degrees and missing one breath in every four. The uncalled debt against the tiles was neither paid nor settled, the coal the brine-gull took on Day 45 was entered in no slate and missed in no account, and another woman lay sixteen mornings uncollected with no word for it.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 13: Days 55--60. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing: salt-stiff coat on its peg, the hollow seat nobody fills, the charred slate in the kiln ash, the clean dark line unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept (T009, T013, T031). His proverb went to the pot and the fire and never to the basket, said over a pot with no crack and a corner where the repair had been rubbed out. The carried fire he first kept lay under blind ash and broken pot at four, four and a gap; the coal the brine-gull took on Day 45 was fifteen days gone, entered in no slate and missed in no account (T088, T065). On Ilmen 29 Sella laid one thumb in his clean dark line and the same thumb in the ridge two doors down and fetched no broom; a barrow of grey went out toward the Bone Orchard at the last market (T013). On Silt 1 a new hairline of grey gathered beside the clean dark line and was called thaw and not swept (T092). The debt against the tiles stayed neither paid nor settled (T009); another woman lay twenty-two mornings uncollected with no word for it.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 14: Days 61–67. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing: the salt-stiff coat held a broader man’s shape on its peg, the hollow seat its twenty-year lean that nobody fills, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash and the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned its corner unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. A new, finer hairline of grey gathered beside it on Silt 2 and lay there all week, unswept and called thaw; the boy set the two lines in two places. His proverb went to a pot with no crack in it over a corner where the repair had been rubbed out. The carried fire under blind ash and broken pot kept four, four and a gap, its payer unnamed and the coal the gull took twenty-two days gone; the debt against the tiles stayed neither paid nor settled while another woman lay twenty-nine mornings uncollected.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 15: Days 68–74, Silt 9–15. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing through the flood and the going of it: salt-stiff coat on its peg, hollow seat nobody fills, charred slate in the kiln ash and clean dark line unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. The Ilm came up over the Fishstairs and stood a hand’s breadth short of that line and of the burned line two doors down, and when it went off into mud neither had been swept; the boy set the standing line, the water that went around it and the new finer grey in three places that did not touch. His proverb went to a pot with no crack over a corner where the repair had been rubbed out. The carried fire under blind ash and broken pot kept four, four and a gap, its payer unnamed and the coal the gull took twenty-nine days gone; the debt against the tiles lay where it lay, neither paid nor settled nor done with, while another woman lay thirty-six mornings uncollected.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 70: Days 261–263, Smoke 22–24. Present in objects only, a keeping and not a story: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg, the hollow wheel-seat, the proverb gone to a pot with no crack, and the debt against a firing of tiles circled without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and sixty-three days; no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Smoke 22, 23 or 24. Tarn kept Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and the ear-sentence came to the word that would call the loan and stopped as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven. The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed for two hundred and sixty-three days; the boy kept the house’s not-doings --- the uncalled loan among them --- as a finding with no payer, held apart from his own kept gaps with a finger between and joined to no absence (T009/T013/T092, T088, T061/T082). No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and sixty-six days; no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Smoke 25, 26 or 27. Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and brought the sentence about an ear worth more than the debt to the calling word on all three days, stopping there as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven. The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed for two hundred and sixty-four, sixty-five and sixty-six days. The boy kept the finding that a thing handled closely still enters nothing on a place of its own, and kept the house’s not-doings apart from his own gaps with a finger between, joining neither to this absence or to any other absence (T009/T013/T092, T088, T061/T082). No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 72: Days 267–269, Smoke 28–30, Eighthday to Tenthday. Present in objects only, a keeping and not a story: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg, the hollow wheel-seat, the proverb gone to a pot with no crack and said over a corner where the repair was rubbed out, and the debt against a firing of tiles circled without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and sixty-nine days; no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Smoke 28, 29 or 30. Tarn kept Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and brought the sentence about an ear worth more than the debt to the calling word on all three days, stopping there as a remembered \textbf{ninth} stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven. The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed for two hundred and sixty-four, sixty-five and sixty-six days gone on to two hundred and sixty-seven, sixty-eight and sixty-nine. Smoke’s third arithmetic went up the road in Berr’s locked box on the 30th and changed nothing under this roof; the boy kept the finding that three readings are three and not one account on a place of its own and did not lay it across this absence or any other (T009/T013/T092, T088, T061/T082, T015/T041/T047). No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and seventy-two days; no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Frost 1, 2 or 3. Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and brought the ear-sentence to the calling word on all three days, stopping there as a remembered \textbf{ninth} stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven. The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed two hundred and seventy through two hundred and seventy-two days; Sella’s opening before the kiln on Frost 2 held the widow’s mark one breath and paid nothing here and made no lesson of four openings in four months. The boy kept the finding that the house’s not-doings and his own gaps stay on separate places for want of a payer, and joined neither to this absence or to any other (T009/T013/T092, T088, T061/T082, T058/T079). No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\end{itemize}
